lessons.titleZh: 以數碼方式廣泛到達手機上

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: New tools can land on everyone's phone.

brief.meaningEn: Become available or arrive on people’s phones, with a context-dependent suggestion of wide reach.
brief.meaningZh: 在大家的手機上出現或變得可用，並按情境帶出廣泛到達的意思。
brief.grammar: A tool/message could land on everyone’s phone; landed is past tense. Everyone refers to the relevant group unless the context establishes a wider claim. Land describes digital arrival, not physical movement.
brief.register: A productive arrival metaphor. The guide gloss links it with widespread adoption, but availability on a phone alone does not establish that its owner chooses to use it.
brief.boundaryZh: 到達或可用與實際採用需要分開；could 也不是已送達，everyone 的範圍要按情境理解。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能把少數人的試用，直接寫成整個群體都已收到、同意使用或有自己的設備。
brief.outcomeZh: 能準確描述數碼到達的可能與範圍，再另行確認使用意願及實際接收。

listening.promptZh: 試用確認了甚麼？甚麼仍未確認？

options.en: Six volunteers could open the tool; wider delivery and other members’ willingness were not yet established.
options.zh: 六位義工能打開工具；更廣泛送達及其他會員的意願，還未確定。

options.en: The trial showed that every member had already chosen the tool for weekly planning.
options.zh: 試用顯示，每位會員都已選用工具作每周規劃。

options.en: The Friday delivery had already happened before the six volunteers tried the tool.
options.zh: 六位義工試用前，周五的送達就已完成。

options.en: The trial had already established how often the other members wanted to use the tool.
options.zh: 試用已確定，其他會員想多久使用一次工具。

listening.explanationZh: 目前知道的是六人能打開工具；其他人的意願及周五前是否送達，仍不是已完成的事。
listening.en: The timetable tool could land on everyone’s phone by Friday, but our trial only showed that six volunteers could open it; we still needed to ask the other club members whether they wanted to use it.
listening.zh: 時間表工具或可在周五前到達全體會員的手機，但試用只顯示六位義工能打開它；我們仍需要問其他會員，是否想使用。

reply.promptEn: Why did you still want to ask the other members?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼仍想詢問其他會員？

options.en: It could land on everyone’s phone without everyone having decided to use it.
options.zh: 即使工具可能到達每人的手機，也不表示每人已決定使用。

options.en: The trial involved six people, not the whole club.
options.zh: 試用涉及六人，不是全體會員。

options.en: Being able to open a tool does not tell us whether it fits someone’s routine.
options.zh: 能打開工具，不會告訴我們它是否配合某人的日常安排。

options.en: We needed to hear their preferences before treating access as agreement.
options.zh: 把可用當作同意之前，我們需要先聽他們的偏好。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出試用範圍與本人選擇仍有分別，不把技術可用當作全體同意。

scene.promptZh: 社團向十人各自的手機發訊息，狀態均顯示「已送達」，但只有兩人回覆是否參加。你只要描述訊息的到達，不推定所有人已讀或答應。哪句最好？

options.en: The message landed on everyone’s phone in that ten-person group, but delivery is not an answer about attendance.
options.zh: 訊息已到達那個十人小組每人的手機，但送達不是出席答覆。

options.en: The delivery status confirms that the other eight people will attend.
options.zh: 送達狀態確認，其餘八人會出席。

options.en: The two replies establish that only two phones received the message.
options.zh: 兩個回覆確立了，只有兩部手機收到訊息。

scene.explanationZh: 送達狀態描述接收，回覆才涉及出席意願；不能把兩項資料互相代替。

contrast.promptZh: 在社團工具的情境中，哪項最不能只從「It could land on everyone’s phone」推論出來？

options.en: The speaker is describing possible digital reach.
options.zh: 說話者正在描述可能的數碼到達範圍。

options.en: The club has already agreed that this will be its sole planning tool.
options.zh: 社團已同意，把它定為唯一規劃工具。

options.en: The context needs to identify which people everyone refers to.
options.zh: 情境需要指出，everyone 指哪些人。

contrast.explanationZh: 可能到達與已同意唯一工具是不同主張；需要另有決定資料。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「六人能開啟，就直接說全體會員已採用吧？」你仍未詢問其他會員。哪個回應最好？

options.en: It could land on everyone’s phone, but our six-person trial does not establish everyone’s choice; let us ask the others.
options.zh: 它可能到達每人的手機，但六人試用不確立每人的選擇；我們先問其他人吧。

options.en: I would make it the default for the whole club now and ask about preferences only after the first week.
options.zh: 我會現在先把它定為全體會員的預設工具，第一周後才問偏好。

options.en: I would use the six people’s ability to open it as confirmation that the rest have already received it.
options.zh: 我會把六人能開啟，當成其餘會員已收到工具的確認。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先按試用實際範圍交代，再詢問未參與者；不以少數人的技術結果代替其他人的接收或選擇。

speaking.en: A new tool may land on everyone’s phone in our group, but I still want to ask who can access it and who chooses to use it.
speaking.zh: 新工具可能到達小組每人的手機，但我仍想問清誰能存取，以及誰選擇使用。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再區分到達、可用及本人決定採用。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替讀書會寫報名說明。有些家庭共用一部手機，成員未必隨時能查看；你想說明，即使通知到達手機，也可以選擇領取紙本，並讓人私下告知需要，而不要求公開家庭情況。用一至兩句英文寫實際說明。

examples.en: The notice may land on everyone’s phone, but a shared device may not be available whenever you need it. You can choose a paper copy and tell me privately which format works for you.
examples.zh: 通知可能到達每人的手機，但共用設備未必隨時可用。你可以選紙本，也可私下告訴我，哪種形式適合你。

examples.en: Even if our update can land on everyone’s phone, we will keep paper copies for anyone who prefers them. Please contact me privately about the format you need; you do not have to explain your household arrangements to the group.
examples.zh: 即使更新可以到達每人的手機，我們仍會為想要的人保留紙本。請私下聯絡我，說明所需形式；你不用向小組解釋家中的安排。

writing.selfCheckZh: 說明要提供可選的接收形式及私下聯絡方法，不以手機送達推定隨時可用，也不要求公開家庭情況。

takeaways.en: The revised address landed on everyone’s phone in the rehearsal group, and the organiser asked for a separate reply about arrival times.
takeaways.zh: 修訂地址到達排練小組每人的手機，主辦者再另問到達時間。

takeaways.en: The guide might land on everyone’s phone before the visit, though the tutor also brought copies for those sharing a device.
takeaways.zh: 到訪前，指引也許會到達每人的手機，但導師也為共用設備的人帶了副本。

review.author: AI author source_inventory

english.evidence: Productive digital-arrival image; exact guide source retained as guide_original_example. Availability/reach is not automatically widespread active adoption, and everyone is bounded to the stated group. Final actual registration notice solves household access/privacy rather than merely repeating the rollout timetable.

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese checked against English subjects, negation, tense and modality; no independent human approval claimed.

lessons.titleZh: 資料呈現另一種解釋

target.pattern: \btell(?:s|ing)? a different story\b|\btold a different story\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Usage data may tell a different story.

brief.meaningEn: Provide evidence for an interpretation that differs from an earlier claim or impression.
brief.meaningZh: 提供支持另一種解釋的資料，與先前主張或印象有所不同。
brief.grammar: The figures/details tell a different story; told in past. Name what the evidence is being compared with. Different need not mean every part of the first account is false.
brief.register: Conventional counter-evidence phrase. Related to tell a story as revealing meaning, but this frame explicitly contrasts an interpretation with another one.
brief.boundaryZh: 資料有差異，不等於已知道差異原因，也不自動表示有人說謊；要指出比較的是哪項主張。
brief.misconceptionZh: 總預約數與實際到場數可以不同，兩者要各自說清，不把其中一項直接當成另一項。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出具體資料怎樣改變解釋，同時保留尚未核實的原因。

listening.promptZh: 入場數據改變了哪個印象？原因是否已知道？

options.en: Attendance was lower than the full bookings suggested, while the reasons still needed checking.
options.zh: 實際到場比滿額預約所暗示的低，原因則仍待核對。

options.en: The entry count confirmed that all one hundred booked places were occupied.
options.zh: 入場點算確認，一百個已預約名額都有使用。

options.en: The organisers had already established that the missing guests disliked the reader.
options.zh: 主辦者已確定，未到場來賓不喜歡朗讀者。

options.en: The booking list contained only forty names before the doors opened.
options.zh: 開門前，預約名單只有四十個名字。

listening.explanationZh: 對比的是預約與實際到場，不是已核實缺席動機；四十是使用名額，不是原本預約總數。
listening.en: The full booking list suggested a packed reading, but the entry count told a different story: only forty of the hundred places were used, and we had not yet asked why the others stayed empty.
listening.zh: 滿額預約名單讓人以為朗讀會座無虛席，但入場點算呈現另一種情況：一百個名額只用了四十個，我們還未問其餘為何空置。

reply.promptEn: Why did you question the impression of a packed room?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼質疑座無虛席的印象？

options.en: The entry count told a different story from the full booking list.
options.zh: 入場點算呈現的情況，與滿額預約名單不同。

options.en: Only forty places were actually used.
options.zh: 實際只用了四十個名額。

options.en: A reservation was not the same as a person arriving.
options.zh: 預約不等於人已到場。

options.en: The evidence about occupied places did not match the impression created by the bookings.
options.zh: 已使用名額的資料，不符合預約所帶來的印象。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以實際到場資料解釋對印象的修正，不補上未核實的缺席原因。

scene.promptZh: 手作班有人只看第一張空桌照片，就說整天沒有人來；逐小時記錄卻顯示下午已有三組參與。哪句準確？

options.en: The later records tell a different story from the claim that the whole day was empty.
options.zh: 較後的記錄呈現的情況，不同於整天無人參與的主張。

options.en: The empty early photograph establishes that the afternoon records also show no visitors.
options.zh: 早段的空桌照片確立了，下午記錄也沒有訪客。

options.en: The afternoon record explains why the table had been empty earlier.
options.zh: 下午記錄解釋了，桌子早段為何空置。

scene.explanationZh: 不同時段可以有不同情況；下午記錄反駁整天無人的推論，但沒有解釋早段為何空置，也不會抹去較後的參與。

contrast.promptZh: 當「The records tell a different story」用來對比先前主張時，哪項最不合適？

options.en: Identify the precise claim that the records challenge.
options.zh: 指出記錄質疑的是哪項具體主張。

options.en: Treat the contrast as proof that the earlier speaker deliberately lied.
options.zh: 把差異當成先前說話者故意說謊的證明。

options.en: Explain which details support the alternative interpretation.
options.zh: 解釋哪些細節支持另一種解釋。

contrast.explanationZh: 資料與主張有差異，不足以自行確定說話者動機或是否故意。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「只有四十人來，就是另外六十人不喜歡朗讀者吧？」你們還未詢問。哪個回應最好？

options.en: The count tells a different story about attendance, but it does not tell us why the other places were empty.
options.zh: 點算呈現不同的到場情況，但沒有告訴我們，其餘名額為何空置。

options.en: I would use the sixty empty places as a measure of how many people disliked the reader.
options.zh: 我會把六十個空置名額，當成不喜歡朗讀者的人數。

options.en: I would keep using the hundred bookings as the attendance figure until the absences are explained.
options.zh: 缺席得到解釋前，我會繼續用一百個預約，當作到場數字。

dialogue.explanationZh: 修正到場數字與追問原因是兩件事；未知動機不會令預約變成實際出席，也不能用空位計算不喜歡的人數。

speaking.en: The details may tell a different story from the first impression, so I want to name what changed and what remains uncertain.
speaking.zh: 細節也許呈現不同於第一印象的情況，所以我想指出，甚麼改變了，以及甚麼仍未確定。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說清楚資料改變哪項解釋。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫小說旁白。人物對同學說自己已不在乎那首被批評的詩，但放學後仍留下逐句改寫，把同學提的問題寫在頁旁。用一至兩句英文呈現她說的話與行動之間的張力，保留她可能有複雜感受，不直接判定她故意騙人。

examples.en: She said the poem no longer mattered, but the questions in the margin of her reworked poem seemed to tell a different story. Alone in the classroom, she was still giving the words her attention.
examples.zh: 她說那首詩已不重要，但修改後詩稿頁邊的問題，似乎呈現另一種情況。獨自在課室裏，她仍把注意力放在那些字句上。

examples.en: Her quiet work after school told a different story from her claim that she no longer cared. Whatever she might later call that feeling, she had stayed to try the poem again.
examples.zh: 放學後安靜改寫的行動，呈現的情況不同於她已不在乎的說法。無論她之後怎樣稱呼那份感受，她都留下來，再試那首詩。

glossary.zh: 把注意力放在那些字句上
她放學後安靜改寫的行動

writing.selfCheckZh: 旁白要以留下改寫及頁旁問題支持張力，不替人物宣布唯一動機或故意說謊；寫出實際場景，而不只解釋詞義。

takeaways.en: The repair log told a different story from the claim that the machine had never failed during the trial.
takeaways.zh: 維修記錄呈現的情況，不同於機器在試用中從未故障的主張。

takeaways.en: Her notes tell a different story about the rehearsal: the long pause was planned, rather than caused by a forgotten line.
takeaways.zh: 她的筆記呈現另一種排練情況：長停頓是有意安排，而不是忘詞造成。

english.evidence: Oxford story entry verifies conventional tell-a-different-story counter-evidence frame. Related672 reveals background; this complementary form explicitly contrasts evidence with a prior interpretation. Final actual fictional narration uses actions/words tension and bounded motive inference rather than another attendance dashboard.

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese checked against English subjects, negation, tense and modality; no independent human approval claimed.

lessons.titleEn: the same stage, but not quite the same dance
lessons.titleZh: 共用一個場域，卻有不同的用法

target.pattern: \bthe same stage, but not quite the same dance\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Families share an app: the same stage, but not quite the same dance.
sources.expression: the same stage, but not quite the same dance

brief.meaningEn: A comparison in which people share a platform or setting but use it in different ways.
brief.meaningZh: 以共用舞台、卻不完全跳同一支舞作比較，形容人們共用平台或場域，卻有不同用法。
brief.grammar: the same stage, but not quite the same dance: + an explanation of the shared setting and differing activities. Stage and dance work together as a creative comparison.
brief.register: A contextual figurative image from the guide, not a standard fixed idiom or a rule about generations. Explain what each part stands for in the particular account.
brief.boundaryZh: 共用平台不表示參與方式、目的或熟練程度相同；不同也不代表其中一方必定用錯。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能只因年齡或身分，就替所有人指定相同用法；要看敘述中的實際行動。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體平台與不同活動支持意象，也能尊重共用空間中的不同需要。

listening.promptZh: 舞台與不同的舞，在這裏分別指甚麼？

options.en: One shared app supported different activities for the two named family members.
options.zh: 同一個共用應用程式，支持兩位已指明家人的不同活動。

options.en: The two relatives relied on separate apps rather than different features within one app.
options.zh: 兩位親人依靠不同應用程式，而不是同一程式內的不同功能。

options.en: Gran used the calendar to arrange every visit, while the brother recorded garden messages.
options.zh: 祖母用日曆安排每次探訪，弟弟則錄花園語音。

options.en: The account described a theatre performance that both relatives were rehearsing.
options.zh: 敘述描述了兩位親人一起排練的舞台演出。

listening.explanationZh: 舞台是共同的應用程式，舞是不同活動；人物與用法不能倒轉，也沒有描述實際演出。
listening.en: In our family app it was the same stage, but not quite the same dance: Gran left voice messages about her garden, while my brother mainly used the calendar to arrange visits; neither use described the whole family.
listening.zh: 在我們的家庭應用程式中，是同一舞台，卻不完全跳同一支舞：祖母用語音分享花園近況，弟弟主要用日曆安排探訪；兩種用法都不能代表全家。

reply.promptEn: Why did the shared app not mean one shared pattern of use?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼共用應用程式，不等於只有一種共同用法？

options.en: It was the same stage, but not quite the same dance: voice messages and planning served different purposes.
options.zh: 是同一舞台，卻不完全跳同一支舞：語音分享與規劃有不同目的。

options.en: The two relatives chose different features for what they wanted to do.
options.zh: 兩位親人按想做的事，選擇不同功能。

options.en: Sharing access did not make their activities identical.
options.zh: 共用存取途徑，沒有令活動變得相同。

options.en: The app held both a garden conversation and arrangements for visits.
options.zh: 應用程式同時容納花園話題，以及探訪安排。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以具體活動說明差異，不把共同平台當成每人目的完全一致。

scene.promptZh: 兩位朋友共用同一間社區工作室，一人在安靜角落修書，另一人在指定時段練習說故事。作者借舞台與舞作比喻，不是在寫真正舞蹈。哪句最貼切？

options.en: It is the same stage, but not quite the same dance: they share a setting while doing different work.
options.zh: 這是同一舞台，卻不完全跳同一支舞：他們共用場域，卻做不同工作。

options.en: Their shared room establishes that both are repairing books in the same way.
options.zh: 共用房間確立了，兩人都以相同方式修書。

options.en: The description concerns two unrelated rooms rather than an arrangement within one studio.
options.zh: 描述關乎兩個沒有關聯的房間，而不是同一工作室內的安排。

scene.explanationZh: 要同時保留共同場域與不同活動；同一房間不會令兩人做相同工作，也不是兩間房。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合這個情境中 the same stage, but not quite the same dance 的用意？

options.en: Identify the shared setting and the different activities.
options.zh: 指出共同場域，以及不同活動。

options.en: Assume one participant’s use defines the only proper use of the shared place.
options.zh: 假定其中一人的用法，就是共用地方唯一正確的用途。

options.en: Use the concrete account rather than assigning habits by age.
options.zh: 按具體敘述理解，而不是按年齡指定習慣。

contrast.explanationZh: 意象用來呈現同中有異，本身沒有判定誰的活動才是唯一正確用法。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「祖母用語音，那就叫弟弟不用日曆，一起改用語音吧？」家庭成員尚未說想改。哪個回應最好？

options.en: It can be the same stage, but not quite the same dance; let us ask which features suit each person instead of assuming one pattern.
options.zh: 可以是同一舞台，卻不完全跳同一支舞；我們先問哪些功能適合各人，而不假定只有一種模式。

options.en: I would remove the calendar so the family’s shared app has one consistent purpose.
options.zh: 我會移除日曆，讓家庭共用程式只有一個一致目的。

options.en: I would treat his calendar entries as evidence that he had listened to all the garden messages.
options.zh: 我會把他的日曆記錄，當成他已聽過所有花園語音的證據。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先承認兩種有目的的用法，再詢問需要；不為表面一致刪去功能，也不從一項功能的使用推定他已看過另一項內容。

speaking.en: We share the same stage, but not quite the same dance: the common space can hold different purposes if we discuss how to use it.
speaking.zh: 我們共用同一舞台，卻不完全跳同一支舞：只要商量怎樣使用，共同空間可以容納不同目的。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說出舞台與舞分別代表的具體事物。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你與哥哥共用餐桌；他晚上需要完成模型，你需要處理工作，不能同時把材料攤滿。你想用這個意象承認兩種用途，再提出商量時段，不說其中一方不該使用餐桌。用一至兩句英文寫實際訊息。

examples.en: We share the same stage, but not quite the same dance: you need the table for your model, while I need it for work. Could we agree separate times instead of treating either use as the only proper one?
examples.zh: 我們共用同一舞台，卻不完全跳同一支舞：你需要餐桌做模型，我則需要用它工作。我們可否商量不同時段，而不把任何一種用法當成唯一正當用途？

examples.en: At this table it is the same stage, but not quite the same dance for us, and both activities need room. Let us work out when each of us can spread our materials out, then leave it clear for the other.
examples.zh: 在這張桌旁，對我們是同一舞台，卻不完全跳同一支舞，兩種活動都需要空間。我們先商量各自何時可以攤開材料，再清好桌面給另一人。

writing.selfCheckZh: 訊息要有共用桌面與不同用途的具體對應，再提出可協商的時段及清理；不把另一用途說成錯誤，也不只寫空泛比喻。

takeaways.en: The shared notebook was the same stage, but not quite the same dance: one member sketched possibilities while another recorded decisions.
takeaways.zh: 共用筆記本是同一舞台，卻不完全跳同一支舞：一位成員畫出可能方案，另一位記下決定。

takeaways.en: For the two visitors it was the same stage, but not quite the same dance, as one studied the building while the other traced a family memory.
takeaways.zh: 對兩位訪客，是同一舞台，卻不完全跳同一支舞；一人研究建築，另一人追尋家人回憶。

lessons.titleZh: 以極快速度

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: News can spread at lightning speed.

brief.meaningEn: Extremely quickly, with lightning serving as a conventional comparison for speed.
brief.meaningZh: 以極快速度進行，以閃電作為速度的慣常比較。
brief.grammar: spread/move/respond at lightning speed; speed is uncountable here. At introduces the speed, and the subject need not be a physical moving object.
brief.register: Established collocation describing very high speed, not a measured claim of matching an electrical discharge.
brief.boundaryZh: 速度快不表示內容正確、所有人跟得上或每一步已完成；要看動作本身及其他資料。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能用傳得快代替來源核對，也不能因一人反應快，就認定別人沒有想法。
brief.outcomeZh: 能形容迅速的行動，並說明速度以外仍需注意的準確性或參與需要。

listening.promptZh: 訊息的速度與準確性，分別有甚麼資料？

options.en: It was forwarded very quickly, but the entrance detail remained outdated and unchecked.
options.zh: 訊息轉發得很快，但入口資料仍過時，也未核對。

options.en: The fast forwarding showed that the entrance had been checked against this year’s map.
options.zh: 迅速轉發顯示，入口已對照今年地圖核實。

options.en: The organisers delayed all forwarding until they had corrected the old entrance information.
options.zh: 主辦者在更正舊入口資料之前，押後了所有轉發。

options.en: The forwarding speed showed that members preferred last year’s entrance.
options.zh: 轉發速度顯示，會員較喜歡去年的入口。

listening.explanationZh: 迅速描述轉發速度，不是核實結果；敘述仍明說舊入口未對照新地圖，也沒有調查會員較喜歡哪個入口。
listening.en: The reminder spread at lightning speed through the festival group: within minutes people were forwarding it, though it still showed last year’s entrance and had not been checked against the new map.
listening.zh: 提醒訊息以極快速度傳遍節慶小組：幾分鐘內大家便在轉發，但上面仍是去年的入口，也還未對照新地圖核實。

reply.promptEn: Why did you call the message’s spread extremely fast?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼說訊息傳播得極快？

options.en: It spread at lightning speed, with people forwarding it within minutes.
options.zh: 它以極快速度傳開，幾分鐘內大家便在轉發。

options.en: There was only a short interval before members passed it on.
options.zh: 會員很快便把它再傳出去。

options.en: The message reached further people through rapid forwarding.
options.zh: 訊息透過迅速轉發，到達更多人。

options.en: People did not wait long before sharing the reminder again.
options.zh: 大家沒有等很久，就再次分享提醒。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以轉發所需時間解釋速度，不把速度當成已核對入口的理由。

scene.promptZh: 朋友很快完成一幅草圖，卻說細部仍想慢慢改；她形容剛才落筆迅速，不是在聲稱已完成最終作品。哪句貼切？

options.en: She drew the first sketch at lightning speed, while leaving the finer details for later work.
options.zh: 她以極快速度畫出第一幅草圖，把較細部分留待之後處理。

options.en: The sketch is ready to be used as the final version without further detail work.
options.zh: 草圖已可當作最終版本使用，不需再處理細部。

options.en: The account says she postponed starting the sketch until all details had been settled.
options.zh: 敘述說，她先定好所有細節，才開始草圖。

scene.explanationZh: 快的是初步草圖，不是最終細部已定；可以把速度與仍待做的工作分開描述。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只從「The answer came at lightning speed」推論出來？

options.en: The response came extremely quickly.
options.zh: 回應來得極快。

options.en: The quick response was necessarily the correct answer.
options.zh: 那個迅速回應，必定就是正確答案。

options.en: The context can show whether the response was later checked.
options.zh: 情境可以顯示，回應之後是否得到核對。

contrast.explanationZh: 這個詞組描述快，不會自行證明對錯；需要另看答案及核對資料。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「傳得那麼快，就沿用入口，不用看新地圖了吧？」訊息仍寫去年的入口。哪個回應最好？

options.en: It spread at lightning speed, but that does not verify the entrance; let us check the new map before forwarding it again.
options.zh: 它傳得極快，但不代表入口已核實；我們再轉發前，先看新地圖吧。

options.en: I would use the number of forwards to decide which entrance to put in the final notice.
options.zh: 我會按轉發次數，決定最後通知寫哪個入口。

options.en: I would wait for someone to report getting lost before comparing the reminder with the map.
options.zh: 我會先等有人說迷路，再把提醒與地圖比較。

dialogue.explanationZh: 對照相關地圖可以核實入口；轉發量及事後等人迷路，都不能代替目前可做的核對。

speaking.en: The ideas came at lightning speed, but I still wanted time to choose which one answered the question we were working on.
speaking.zh: 想法來得極快，但我仍想有時間選擇，哪一個回答了我們正在處理的問題。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清想法的速度與選擇哪個有用的需要。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友腦力激盪時接連提出很多新構想，你還未回答一個，他已轉到下一個。你想肯定他的活力，也請求先記下新構想、一起選一個討論，讓雙方能參與，不把速度慢說成沒有想法。用一至兩句英文實際回覆。

examples.en: Your ideas come at lightning speed, and I would like time to answer one before we move to the next. Could we write the new ideas down and choose one together?
examples.zh: 你的想法來得極快，而我想有時間回應一個，再轉到下一個。我們可否先記下新構想，再一起選一個？

examples.en: We are moving at lightning speed, and I am glad there are so many possibilities. Could we pause over one idea so I can contribute, while keeping a note of the others for later?
examples.zh: 我們進行得極快，我很高興有那麼多可能。我們可否先停在一個構想，讓我也能參與，同時記下其他構想，留待之後？

writing.selfCheckZh: 回覆要承認構想的活力，再提出具體參與方法；不把快速直接當成每個構想都好，也不把需要時間當成沒有貢獻。

takeaways.en: She sorted the familiar cards at lightning speed, then slowed down to read the handwritten note she did not recognise.
takeaways.zh: 她以極快速度整理熟悉卡片，再放慢讀一則不認得的手寫筆記。

takeaways.en: The invitation travelled at lightning speed through the choir, while decisions about the rehearsal date still needed replies.
takeaways.zh: 邀請極快傳遍合唱團，但決定排練日期仍需要回覆。

lessons.titleZh: 事件尚待補充修訂的初步記錄

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Social feeds often provide the first draft of events.

brief.meaningEn: An early, provisional account of what happened that may need checking, context or correction.
brief.meaningZh: 對已發生事情的初步記錄，之後可能需要核對、補充背景或更正。
brief.grammar: describe/treat something as the first draft of events. Draft compares early reporting with writing that can still be revised; events refers to the happenings being described.
brief.register: A contextual reporting metaphor in the guide, not a claim that early accounts are always false or later accounts automatically reliable.
brief.boundaryZh: 初步不表示全錯；後來更完整，也仍要有來源支持。要分清當時已知、尚待查問及已更正的部分。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能因稱為初稿，就把已造成的錯誤影響抹去；也不應不加說明地讓過時版本繼續流傳。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明初步敘述的限制，以及新資料怎樣補充或更正它。

listening.promptZh: 後來資料補充了甚麼？哪部分仍未確定？

options.en: The reading continued indoors, while the time of that move was still unconfirmed.
options.zh: 朗讀在室內繼續，但移動時間仍未確認。

options.en: The first post had already explained the indoor continuation and the exact time.
options.zh: 第一則帖文已解釋室內繼續的情況，以及確切時間。

options.en: The later interviews established that no outdoor reading had started at all.
options.zh: 後來訪問確立了，戶外朗讀根本沒有開始。

options.en: The later account removed the need to check any timing details.
options.zh: 後來敘述已免除核對時間細節的需要。

listening.explanationZh: 後來資料補上移到室內，不是活動從未開始；時間仍待核對，不能把後來敘述當成全已確認。
listening.en: The first post was the first draft of events: it said the outdoor reading had stopped, but later interviews showed that the group had moved inside; the time of the move still needed checking.
listening.zh: 第一則帖文是事件的初步記錄：它說戶外朗讀停止了，但後來訪問顯示，小組已移到室內；移動時間則仍需要核對。

reply.promptEn: Why did you describe the first post as provisional?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼把第一則帖文形容為初步記錄？

options.en: It was the first draft of events, missing the continuation that later interviews added.
options.zh: 它是事件的初步記錄，缺少了後來訪問補上的繼續情況。

options.en: It reported the outdoor stop without the move indoors.
options.zh: 它報告戶外活動停止，沒有交代移到室內。

options.en: New information changed how the interruption should be understood.
options.zh: 新資料改變了，應怎樣理解那次中斷。

options.en: Its account needed more context before readers could understand what happened to the reading.
options.zh: 讀者理解朗讀會後來怎樣之前，那份敘述仍需要更多背景。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出初步敘述缺少的具體部分，而不是只用初稿一詞否定全部。

scene.promptZh: 社區刊物先刊出一位目擊者所見的開門情況，清楚標示另一入口仍待查問；編輯之後會比較其他人的記錄。哪句貼切？

options.en: The report can be treated as the first draft of events, with its present limits made clear.
options.zh: 報道可以視為事件的初步記錄，並說清楚目前限制。

options.en: Calling it a draft establishes that the eyewitness’s description of the observed entrance is false.
options.zh: 稱它為初稿，就確立目擊者對所見入口的描述是假的。

options.en: The label means that the other entrance has already been checked and added.
options.zh: 這個標示表示，另一入口已查問並補上。

scene.explanationZh: 初步狀態與清楚標示限制可以並存；不代表已見部分全錯，也不等於待查部分已補齊。

contrast.promptZh: 在報道的比喻中，哪項最不符合 the first draft of events 的用意？

options.en: Distinguish the current account from facts still being checked.
options.zh: 把目前敘述，與仍待核對的事情分開。

options.en: Assume the next edited account must be correct merely because it is later.
options.zh: 只因下一份編輯後敘述較遲出現，就假定它必定正確。

options.en: Explain what a later correction adds or changes.
options.zh: 解釋後來更正補充或改變了甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 初稿的比喻保留修訂空間，不會把較遲出現直接當成可靠性的證明。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「第一帖只寫戶外朗讀停止，既然只是初稿，就不用標出已移到室內繼續的新資料吧？」第一帖仍有人轉傳。哪個回應最好？

options.en: It was the first draft of events, so we should link a clear update explaining the continuation rather than leave readers with the old impression.
options.zh: 它是事件的初步記錄，所以應連上一則清楚更新，交代活動繼續，而不讓讀者只留下舊印象。

options.en: I would post the indoor photograph without explaining how it changes the earlier report.
options.zh: 我會只貼室內照片，不解釋它怎樣改變先前報道。

options.en: I would wait until every timing detail is settled before telling readers that the reading continued.
options.zh: 我會等每項時間細節都確定，才告訴讀者朗讀已繼續。

dialogue.explanationZh: 已核實的繼續情況可以清楚更新，同時標示時間仍待查；不必含糊貼圖或把可更正的資料全部押後。

speaking.en: This is the first draft of events, so I want to mark what we know now and explain any later correction clearly.
speaking.zh: 這是事件的初步記錄，所以我想標明目前知道甚麼，也把之後的更正說清楚。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明初步記錄與更正責任怎樣相連。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替社團寫更正啟事。先前初步消息錯稱義工遲送物料；已核對的收貨記錄顯示他準時到，但倉庫未開。你要承認錯誤、交代更正依據並連結更新，不把「初稿」當成不需道歉的理由。用一至兩句英文寫實際啟事。

examples.en: Our earlier post was the first draft of events, but it unfairly described the volunteer as late, and we apologise. The checked delivery record shows he arrived on time while the storeroom was closed; we have linked the correction to the original post.
examples.zh: 先前帖文是事件的初步記錄，但不公平地說義工遲到，我們為此道歉。已核對的送貨記錄顯示，他準時到達，當時倉庫未開；我們已把更正連到原帖。

examples.en: We treated an unverified message as the first draft of events and wrongly blamed the volunteer for a delay. We are sorry: the checked record confirms his arrival on time, and our update now explains that the storeroom had not opened.
examples.zh: 我們把一則未核實訊息當作事件的初步記錄，卻錯怪義工造成延誤。對不起：已核對的記錄確認他準時到達，更新現在已交代，當時倉庫還未開。

writing.selfCheckZh: 啟事要承認具體錯誤及對人的影響，交代已核對依據與可見更新；不以初步狀態免除更正，也不把未開倉庫寫成義工遲到。

takeaways.en: The hurried diary entry was the first draft of events, and she returned to the timetable before quoting it in her memoir.
takeaways.zh: 匆忙寫下的日記是事件的初步記錄，她在回憶錄引用前，先回頭核對時間表。

takeaways.en: He labelled the recording the first draft of events and invited the other witnesses to add what they had actually seen.
takeaways.zh: 他把錄音標示為事件的初步記錄，並邀請其他目擊者補充自己實際所見。

lessons.titleZh: 經選取與整理的敘述版本

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A newspaper may provide the edited version.

brief.meaningEn: A version of an account shaped by editing; in the reporting comparison, a more worked-over account than the initial reports.
brief.meaningZh: 經編輯處理的敘述版本；在報道的比較中，指比初步消息經過更多整理的版本。
brief.grammar: provide/read/check the edited version of an account. Editing may involve selection, checking, context or wording; the surrounding evidence establishes which changes were made.
brief.register: Ordinary editing language used within the guide’s draft/version image for reporting. The phrase alone does not certify accuracy or establish that print is always more reliable than a social post.
brief.boundaryZh: 編輯過不等於每項內容已核實；需要看實際改動、來源與保留的意思，也不表示被刪的內容必定不重要。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要只按媒體形式判可靠，也不要把較流暢的文字直接當成更完整或更忠於原意。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出版本經過哪些整理，並按具體資料檢查它是否保留重要限制。

listening.promptZh: 這個版本做了哪些整理？哪部分仍未確定？

options.en: It checked timing accounts and corrected a name, while keeping one quotation visibly unconfirmed.
options.zh: 它比較時間敘述並更正姓名，同時清楚保留一句引言未確認的狀態。

options.en: It confirmed that both witnesses gave exactly the same time before correcting the organiser’s name.
options.zh: 它先確認兩位目擊者所說的時間完全相同，再更正主辦者姓名。

options.en: It kept the organiser’s earlier name unchanged and did not compare the witnesses.
options.zh: 它保留主辦者原來的姓名，也沒有比較目擊者。

options.en: The revised report treated the remaining quotation as confirmed once the organiser’s name was corrected.
options.zh: 更正主辦者姓名後，修訂報道便把餘下引言當成已確認。

listening.explanationZh: 比較時間不等於已確認兩人所說的時間完全相同；已更正的是主辦者姓名，而引言仍未確認。流暢或其他細節已核對，都不能代替引言本身的核實。
listening.en: The edited version compared two witnesses’ times and corrected the name of the organiser, but the reporter still marked one quotation as unconfirmed instead of making the smoother account sound final.
listening.zh: 編輯後的版本比較了兩位目擊者的時間，並更正主辦者姓名，但記者仍把一句引言標為未確認，沒有讓較流暢的敘述聽來已成定論。

reply.promptEn: What work had gone into the revised report?
reply.promptZh: 修訂報道經過哪些處理？

options.en: The edited version compared the witness accounts and corrected the organiser’s name.
options.zh: 編輯後的版本比較目擊者敘述，並更正主辦者姓名。

options.en: The reporter had checked the timing information from two people.
options.zh: 記者已比較兩人的時間資料。

options.en: A name had been corrected, while the uncertain quotation stayed labelled.
options.zh: 一個姓名已更正，不確定的引言則仍有標示。

options.en: The wording was smoother, but the account still showed where confirmation was missing.
options.zh: 措辭較流暢，但敘述仍顯示哪些部分缺少確認。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述實際編輯或標示工作，不把整個版本說成所有疑點已解決。

scene.promptZh: 編輯只調整段落順序與字距，沒有查問任何來源；有人說「編輯後的版本」這個名稱已證明引言真確。哪句最準確？

options.en: Calling it the edited version does not establish that the quotation was checked; the stated changes concern presentation.
options.zh: 稱它為編輯後版本，不確立引言已核對；已說明的改動關乎呈現方式。

options.en: The new paragraph order confirms that the quoted speaker approved the wording.
options.zh: 新的段落順序，確認被引述者已同意措辭。

options.en: The description says the editor compared the quotation with the original recording.
options.zh: 描述說，編輯已把引言與原始錄音比較。

scene.explanationZh: 按實際做過的工作判斷；重排與字距不會提供被引述者確認或錄音核對的證據。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只從「This is the edited version」得出？

options.en: Some editing has shaped the account.
options.zh: 敘述經過某些編輯處理。

options.en: The label establishes that the account is more accurate than a named earlier version.
options.zh: 這個標示確立了，敘述比某個較早版本更準確。

options.en: The actual changes need to be examined to judge their effect.
options.zh: 要判斷改動的影響，需要查看實際處理。

contrast.explanationZh: 版本名稱說明經過編輯，不會自行比較準確性；需要看改了甚麼及依據。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「行文順了，那句未確認引言的標示可以刪吧？」記者仍未收到說話者確認。哪個回應最好？

options.en: The edited version is smoother, but that does not confirm the quotation; I would keep its status clear.
options.zh: 編輯後版本較流暢，但不代表引言已確認；我會繼續說清它的狀態。

options.en: I would treat the smoother wording as enough evidence to publish the quotation without that label.
options.zh: 我會把較流暢的措辭，當成可以不加標示刊出引言的充分依據。

options.en: I would put the quotation first because the other checked details make it seem reliable enough.
options.zh: 我會把引言放在首段，因為其他已核對細節，令它看來已足夠可靠。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可改善文字，同時保留來源狀態；位置、流暢度或其他細節已核對，都不能代替這句引言缺少的確認。

speaking.en: I want to compare the edited version with the original account before deciding whether an important qualification has been lost.
speaking.zh: 決定是否遺漏重要限制之前，我想把編輯後版本與原來敘述比較。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出需要比較哪個限制或資料來源。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你受訪時說「若試用結果合適，我們可能延長開放時間」，校刊整理稿卻刪去條件與「可能」，變成已決定延長。你想向編輯要求恢復準確意思，不要求照登所有口頭重複。用一至兩句英文實際回覆。

examples.en: The edited version makes the longer opening hours sound decided, but I said they depended on the trial. Could you restore that condition and the word “may”, while keeping the rest concise?
examples.zh: 編輯後版本令延長開放時間聽來已定案，但我說的是要看試用結果。你可否恢復那個條件及「可能」，其餘部分仍保持簡潔？

examples.en: Please keep the uncertainty in the edited version: we may extend the hours if the trial supports it. I am happy for you to remove repetition, but not to turn that possibility into an announcement.
examples.zh: 請在編輯後版本保留不確定性：如果試用結果支持，我們可能延長時間。我接受刪去重複，但不應把可能性變成宣布。

writing.selfCheckZh: 回覆要指出被刪條件及可能性怎樣改變意思，要求準確但可簡潔的呈現；不把編輯一概當成造假，也不把口頭每字保留當唯一忠實方式。

takeaways.en: The edited version restored the speaker’s “if”, so readers could see that the plan depended on permission.
takeaways.zh: 編輯後版本恢復了說話者的「如果」，讓讀者看見計劃取決於許可。

takeaways.en: She checked the edited version against her notes and asked why a question had been presented as a decision.
takeaways.zh: 她把編輯後版本與筆記比較，並問為甚麼一條問題被寫成已作的決定。

lessons.titleEn: throwing a dramatic headline at people
lessons.titleZh: 把誇張標題猛然拋給讀者

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Responsible news avoids throwing a dramatic headline at people.
sources.expression: throwing a dramatic headline at people

brief.meaningEn: Present a striking or sensational headline abruptly, especially without enough context for readers to understand it.
brief.meaningZh: 突然把強烈或誇張的標題放到讀者面前，尤其缺少足夠背景讓人理解。
brief.grammar: throw/throwing a dramatic headline at people; threw in past. Throw is figurative presentation, and the following context explains what is missing or why the presentation is abrupt.
brief.register: A productive throwing-information image, not a fixed technical category for all short headlines. Dramatic wording may be justified by events, but should not replace necessary context.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是任何短標題或強烈用語都一定誤導；需要比較它給的印象與已有事實。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把標題吸引注意的能力，當成它已讓讀者理解情況；也不因反對誇張就把真正重要消息藏起來。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出標題缺少哪項背景，並提出有目的的敘述或查問方式。

listening.promptZh: 標題漏了甚麼背景？較完整通知交代了甚麼？

options.en: The headline omitted the limited room and duration, while the notice explained the repair and continuing access.
options.zh: 標題漏了有限房間及期限，通知則解釋維修與仍可進入的部分。

options.en: The notice confirmed that the whole library would be permanently closed.
options.zh: 通知確認，整間圖書館會永久關閉。

options.en: The headline already stated the exact room and two-day period.
options.zh: 標題已列明確切房間及兩天期限。

options.en: The repair concerned all the rooms that the notice described as remaining open.
options.zh: 維修涉及通知說仍開放的所有房間。

listening.explanationZh: 差別在影響範圍及時間；較完整通知沒有把局部維修變成全館永久關閉。
listening.en: The post was throwing a dramatic headline at people with “Library closes”, while leaving out that only one room would shut for two days; the notice underneath explained the repair and the rooms that remained open.
listening.zh: 帖文用「圖書館關閉」把誇張標題拋給讀者，卻漏了只是其中一個房間關閉兩天；下方通知則解釋維修，以及哪些房間仍開放。

reply.promptEn: Why did you find the headline misleading?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼覺得標題容易誤導？

options.en: It was throwing a dramatic headline at people without naming the limited closure.
options.zh: 它把誇張標題拋給讀者，沒有指出關閉只限部分範圍。

options.en: Readers could take it as a closure of the whole library.
options.zh: 讀者可能把它當成整間圖書館關閉。

options.en: The two-day limit and the room still mattered to the meaning.
options.zh: 兩天期限及是哪個房間，仍會影響意思。

options.en: The notice contained a narrower explanation than the title suggested.
options.zh: 通知的解釋範圍，比標題所暗示的窄。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明標題印象與具體範圍的差距，不是只因字少就斷定有問題。

scene.promptZh: 一則短標題清楚寫「東閱覽室周二、周三維修」，下方也有其他開放區域及來源。讀者只因它短，就說這一定是把誇張標題拋給人。哪句最準確？

options.en: Brevity alone does not show that the writer is throwing a dramatic headline at people without context; the scope and source are stated.
options.zh: 簡短本身不足以顯示，作者正缺少背景地把誇張標題拋給讀者；範圍與來源都已說明。

options.en: The short title establishes that the writer concealed the repair dates.
options.zh: 標題簡短，足以確立作者隱瞞了維修日期。

options.en: The short title reports that the closure affects the whole library rather than one room.
options.zh: 短標題報告，關閉涉及整間圖書館，而不是一個房間。

scene.explanationZh: 要看是否交代必要範圍與來源，而不只看長短；這裏日期與房間已清楚列出。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合「避免 throwing a dramatic headline at people」的提醒？

options.en: Include the limitation that changes how readers understand the event.
options.zh: 加入會改變讀者理解事件的限制。

options.en: Choose the strongest reaction first and leave readers to discover the scope for themselves.
options.zh: 先選最強烈的反應，把範圍留給讀者自行發現。

options.en: Keep an important warning clear while giving its relevant context.
options.zh: 清楚保留重要提醒，也交代相關背景。

contrast.explanationZh: 提醒是讓注意力與理解相連，不是讓讀者只剩強烈反應，也不是要求隱去重要消息。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「只要很多人按進來，關哪一間就放最後再說。」你想讓標題本身先給準確範圍。哪個回應最好？

options.en: I would rather name the two-day room closure than keep throwing a dramatic headline at people and hoping they find the limit later.
options.zh: 我寧願先列明房間關閉兩天，也不想一直把誇張標題拋給讀者，再希望他們之後找到限制。

options.en: I would keep the broad closure claim in the title and use clicks as the test of whether it is clear.
options.zh: 我會把廣泛關閉的說法留在標題，再用點擊數判斷它是否清楚。

options.en: I would remove the room name from the summary so readers have to open the post to learn the scope.
options.zh: 我會把房間名稱從摘要刪去，讓讀者必須打開帖文才知道範圍。

dialogue.explanationZh: 把影響意思的範圍放清楚，比用點擊量或刻意留白來代替理解更貼合目的。

speaking.en: I do not want to keep throwing dramatic headlines at people; I want the important point and its limits to be clear together.
speaking.zh: 我不想一直把誇張標題拋給讀者；我想同時說清重要重點及限制。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出哪些限制應與重點一起出現。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你向校刊編輯提議介紹一場學生演出。與其只用失誤片段作聳動標題，你想訪問表演者與幕後同學，交代道具倒下後怎樣接續演出，也保留他們不同感受。用一至兩句英文提出具體採訪方案，不聲稱有失誤就不能報道。

examples.en: Instead of throwing a dramatic headline at people about the fallen prop, I would like to interview a performer and someone backstage about how the scene continued. Could we give room to both accounts rather than let one clip define the whole performance?
examples.zh: 與其把道具倒下寫成誇張標題拋給讀者，我想訪問一位表演者及一位幕後同學，了解場景怎樣繼續。我們可否容納兩份敘述，而不讓一段影片定義整場演出？

examples.en: We can report the mistake without throwing dramatic headlines at people as the whole story. I propose a short feature comparing what the performer and backstage helper noticed when they kept the scene going.
examples.zh: 我們可以報道失誤，而不把誇張標題當成整個故事拋給讀者。我提議做一篇短專題，比較表演者及幕後幫手接續場景時，各自留意到甚麼。

writing.selfCheckZh: 方案要提出實際訪問對象及比較問題，保留失誤與後續行動的完整範圍；不以吸引點擊代替理解，也不要求隱去失誤。

takeaways.en: The editor rejected throwing a dramatic headline at people and asked the reporter to state which part of the route was affected.
takeaways.zh: 編輯不採用把誇張標題拋給讀者的做法，要求記者說清楚路線哪部分受影響。

takeaways.en: She avoided throwing dramatic headlines at people by putting the agreed facts beside the warning, rather than hiding the issue.
takeaways.zh: 她把已確認事實放在提醒旁邊，而不是隱去問題，避免把誇張標題猛然拋給讀者。

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese checked against English subjects, negation, tense and modality; no independent human approval claimed.

lessons.titleZh: 為吸引點擊而截取的零碎片段

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Readers deserve more than click-worthy fragments.

brief.meaningEn: Short selected pieces shaped to attract clicks, which may leave out context needed for understanding.
brief.meaningZh: 為吸引點擊而挑選的短片段，可能漏去理解所需的背景。
brief.grammar: click-worthy fragments of an interview/event; click-worthy is a productive hyphenated adjective, and fragments names incomplete pieces of a wider account.
brief.register: A natural digital-media phrase rather than an opaque fixed idiom. The guide places it under set phrases; its component meanings remain transparent.
brief.boundaryZh: 短不一定失真，吸引點擊也不必然不誠實；要看片段省略甚麼，以及有沒有清楚通往所需背景。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能把觀看量當成充分理解，也不應因反對零碎片段，就認為有用資訊只能以很長文章提供。
brief.outcomeZh: 能檢查短內容保留哪些必要資料，並提出兼顧簡潔與理解的安排。

listening.promptZh: 截取方式漏了甚麼？怎樣影響意思？

options.en: It omitted the qualification that the change was only proposed, making it seem confirmed.
options.zh: 它漏了改動只是提議的限制，令事情看似已確認。

options.en: It retained the speaker’s full explanation that no decision had been made.
options.zh: 它保留說話者完整解釋，說明還未作決定。

options.en: The speaker announced that the proposal had become a final decision during the clip.
options.zh: 說話者在影片中宣布，提議已成最終決定。

options.en: The startled reaction was added after the speaker had already finished the qualification.
options.zh: 驚訝反應是在說話者已解釋完限制後才加上的。

listening.explanationZh: 已知問題是片段結束得太早，漏了提議而非定案的差別；不是片段已保留完整限制。
listening.en: The interview became click-worthy fragments in the feed: the clip kept the startled reaction but ended before the speaker explained that the change was only a proposal, making the plan sound decided.
listening.zh: 訪問在動態中變成吸引點擊的零碎片段：影片保留驚訝反應，卻在說話者解釋改動只是提議前結束，令計劃聽來已定案。

reply.promptEn: Why was the short clip insufficient for understanding the plan?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼單看短片，還不足以理解計劃？

options.en: The click-worthy fragments left out that the change was only a proposal.
options.zh: 吸引點擊的零碎片段，漏了改動只是提議的資訊。

options.en: The reaction was shown without the qualification that followed it.
options.zh: 片段展示反應，沒有其後的限制說明。

options.en: Readers could mistake a possibility for an announced decision.
options.zh: 讀者可能把一個可能，誤當成已宣布的決定。

options.en: The selected ending changed the apparent status of the plan.
options.zh: 選取的結尾，改變了計劃看來的狀態。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出具體缺口及意思影響，不是單憑短或受歡迎就否定內容。

scene.promptZh: 一則短摘要清楚寫「委員會仍在討論」，並連到完整訪問，沒有把它寫成已通過。有人只因字少，就說它只能是誤導的點擊片段。哪句最好？

options.en: A brief summary can offer more than click-worthy fragments when it keeps the decision status clear and provides the fuller account.
options.zh: 短摘要只要保留清楚的決定狀態，也提供較完整敘述，就可以不只提供吸引點擊的零碎片段。

options.en: A short summary establishes that the writer has hidden the fact that discussion continues.
options.zh: 短摘要足以確立，作者隱瞞了討論仍在進行。

options.en: The summary says the proposal was approved before the interview took place.
options.zh: 摘要說，訪問進行前，提議就已通過。

scene.explanationZh: 要按有沒有保留影響意思的資訊判斷；這裏仍在討論，沒有說提議已通過。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合檢查 click-worthy fragments 時應注意的事？

options.en: Ask which qualification the selection leaves out.
options.zh: 問選取過程漏了哪個限制。

options.en: Use the number of clicks as evidence that the audience understood the decision correctly.
options.zh: 用點擊數，當成觀眾已正確理解決定的證據。

options.en: Compare the excerpt with the relevant surrounding explanation.
options.zh: 把節錄與相關的前後解釋比較。

contrast.explanationZh: 點擊是互動數字，不是理解正確的直接證據；需要看內容及所需背景。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「短片很多人看，就不用補提議尚未通過吧？」你想保留片段，也說清狀態。哪個回應最好？

options.en: The click-worthy fragments can attract attention, but we should add that the change is still a proposal and link the explanation.
options.zh: 吸引點擊的零碎片段可以引起注意，但我們應補上改動仍是提議，並連到解釋。

options.en: I would treat the viewing figures as proof that people already know no decision was made.
options.zh: 我會把觀看數字，當成人們已知道還未作決定的證明。

options.en: I would remove the reaction but leave the plan sounding confirmed, since then the clip would be less dramatic.
options.zh: 我會刪去驚訝反應，但仍讓計劃聽來已定案，因為那樣影片便沒那麼戲劇化。

dialogue.explanationZh: 關鍵是保留提議狀態，不只減少戲劇感或增加觀看數字；可同時提供片段與所需背景。

speaking.en: I want more than click-worthy fragments when a missing qualification changes what the speaker seems to have agreed to.
speaking.zh: 若漏去一個限制會改變說話者看來同意了甚麼，我想看到的不只是吸引點擊的零碎片段。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出哪項限制會改變整體意思。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們要為手機讀者做一則很短的活動介紹。你想保留日期、地點與是否需要報名，另連完整節目表，不把簡潔寫成只能剩煽動片段。用一至兩句英文向同伴提出可行的內容安排。

examples.en: We can offer a short event summary rather than only click-worthy fragments: the date, place and registration requirement should stay visible. Let’s link the full programme for readers who want the details.
examples.zh: 我們可以提供簡短活動摘要，而不只剩吸引點擊的零碎片段：日期、地點及是否需要報名，應保持可見。讓我們連到完整節目表，給想看詳情的讀者。

examples.en: I would keep the essential event information in the short version, not reduce it to click-worthy fragments. A clear link to the programme can offer more detail without making the basic arrangements hard to find.
examples.zh: 我會把必要活動資訊留在短版本，不把它縮成吸引點擊的零碎片段。清楚的節目表連結可以提供更多詳情，同時不讓基本安排變得難找。

writing.selfCheckZh: 提出簡潔而保留必要資訊的實際安排，也給願看詳情的人清楚途徑；不把短內容一概否定，或讓讀者必須點開才知道基本安排。

takeaways.en: The profile offered more than click-worthy fragments by keeping the speaker’s reservation beside the striking quote.
takeaways.zh: 人物專訪不只提供吸引點擊的零碎片段，也把說話者的保留意見放在醒目引言旁。

takeaways.en: He compared the click-worthy fragments with the full recording before deciding what the speaker had actually promised.
takeaways.zh: 他把吸引點擊的零碎片段與完整錄音比較，再判斷說話者實際答應了甚麼。

Main omitted proposal qualification, inverse scene accurate short summary, final actionable concise-event information design balances brevity, essential facts and optional detail.

lessons.titleZh: 只靠過去名聲維持下去

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Traditional outlets cannot live on reputation alone.

brief.meaningEn: Depend on an established reputation for continuing support, rather than demonstrate the current work on which that support could also be based.
brief.meaningZh: 依靠已有名聲維持支持，而不是展示也可作為支持依據的當前工作。
brief.grammar: cannot/should not live on reputation alone; a publication, organisation or person can be the subject. Alone limits the basis of support rather than denying that reputation has any value.
brief.register: Conventional dependence-on-reputation expression. The guide’s negative sentence warns against relying only on prestige, not against acknowledging a real record of achievement.
brief.boundaryZh: 名聲有價值，卻不能自行證明當前服務或作品仍合需要；cannot 的提醒不表示已倒閉或從來沒有成就。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能因反對只靠名聲，就抹去過去的好工作；也不能把舊獎項當成今天已核對內容的證據。
brief.outcomeZh: 能保留過往成就，也指出當前仍需做甚麼來維持信任或參與。

listening.promptZh: 舊成就與當前工作，有甚麼關係？

options.en: The awards remained valuable, but current reporting and corrections were still needed.
options.zh: 獎項仍有價值，但仍需要當前報道及更正工作。

options.en: The speaker said the old awards had never represented any worthwhile work.
options.zh: 說話者說，舊獎項從未代表任何有價值的工作。

options.en: Repeating the prize list was presented as enough to check each new local claim.
options.zh: 重複得獎名單，被描述成足以核實每項新的本地主張。

options.en: The paper had already closed and the account concerned only its final sale.
options.zh: 報章已停辦，敘述只關乎最後出售。

listening.explanationZh: 提醒針對只靠名聲，不是否定過去，也不是報告已停辦；核實新資料需要當前工作。
listening.en: The local paper could not live on reputation alone: its old awards mattered, but readers still needed clear corrections and checked local reports, not simply the same prize list beside every new article.
listening.zh: 本地報章不能只靠過去名聲維持：舊獎項有價值，但讀者仍需要清楚更正及已核實的本地報道，而不只是每篇新文章旁邊重貼得獎名單。

reply.promptEn: Why did the paper still need checked reports and clear corrections?
reply.promptZh: 報章為甚麼仍需要核實報道及清楚更正？

options.en: It could not live on reputation alone; readers needed evidence of present care.
options.zh: 它不能只靠過去名聲維持；讀者需要看見當前的用心及依據。

options.en: Old awards did not check the facts in each new article.
options.zh: 舊獎項沒有核實每篇新文章的事實。

options.en: Trust needed support from what the paper was doing now.
options.zh: 信任需要報章現在所做的工作支持。

options.en: A prize list could record past achievement without answering current readers’ questions.
options.zh: 得獎名單可以記錄過去成就，卻不會回答當前讀者的問題。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出當前品質與舊成就不同，不把名聲當成沒有價值，也不讓它代做新工作。

scene.promptZh: 一間多年有口碑的修理店，仍逐件檢查新送來物品、清楚解釋限制及跟進結果。評論只因它有舊名聲，就說一定只靠名聲。哪句最好？

options.en: Having a reputation does not show that the shop is trying to live on reputation alone when current careful work is described.
options.zh: 敘述有當前細心工作時，有名聲不表示店舖正只靠名聲維持。

options.en: Mentioning its history establishes that the shop no longer checks new repairs.
options.zh: 提及歷史，就確立店舖不再檢查新維修。

options.en: The checks took place only when the shop first earned its reputation, not on the newly delivered items.
options.zh: 檢查只在店舖最初建立名聲時進行，不是針對新送來的物品。

scene.explanationZh: 要看是否只靠名聲；這裏明說逐件檢查新送來物品，當前工作與過去好紀錄可以並存。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合「We cannot live on reputation alone」的提醒？

options.en: Recognise earlier achievements while checking current standards.
options.zh: 承認早期成就，也檢視當前標準。

options.en: Treat past prestige as a substitute for asking whether the present work meets people’s needs.
options.zh: 把過去名望當成替代品，不再問當前工作是否符合需要。

options.en: Identify what present action would support continuing trust.
options.zh: 指出哪些當前行動可支持持續信任。

contrast.explanationZh: 提醒是讓當前表現支持信任，不是只陳列過往名聲或否定所有舊成就。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「得過獎，就不用公開今天那則更正，讀者自然會信吧？」你仍有一個已確認的錯誤要更正。哪個回應最好？

options.en: We cannot live on reputation alone; a clear correction is part of earning trust in what we publish now.
options.zh: 我們不能只靠過去名聲維持；清楚更正，是讓現在刊出的內容值得信任的一部分。

options.en: I would put the award list beside the article instead of showing readers what changed.
options.zh: 我會把得獎名單放在文章旁，而不向讀者說明改了甚麼。

options.en: I would revise the wording quietly and let the old awards stand as the explanation for why readers can trust it.
options.zh: 我會悄悄修改措辭，仍以舊獎項解釋讀者為何可相信它。

dialogue.explanationZh: 更正回應的是當前已知錯誤；只列得獎名單或悄悄改字，都沒有向讀者清楚交代變更。

speaking.en: Our group cannot live on reputation alone, so we want newcomers to see how we work now rather than only hear what we won before.
speaking.zh: 團體不能只靠過去名聲維持，所以我們想讓新來者看見現在怎樣做，而不只聽以前贏過甚麼。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把當前做法與舊成就分清。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你的樂團以往得過獎，但新成員第一次排練時看不懂舊樂譜記號，也不知道何時可提問。你想在成員會上提議一次簡短導入及固定提問時段，讓新來者真正能參與，不取消舊團員的成就。用一至兩句英文提出建議。

examples.en: We cannot live on reputation alone if new members cannot follow the markings or find a moment to ask. Could we begin with a short guide to the score and set aside time for their questions?
examples.zh: 如果新成員看不懂記號，也找不到時間發問，我們便不能只靠過去名聲維持。我們可否先簡短介紹樂譜，並留時間回答他們的問題？

examples.en: The awards are worth celebrating, but the band cannot live on reputation alone. A brief introduction to our markings and a regular question time would help newcomers take part in the work behind that record.
examples.zh: 獎項值得慶祝，但樂團不能只靠過去名聲維持。簡短介紹記號，加上固定提問時間，可幫新來者參與支撐那份紀錄的實際工作。

glossary.en: a short guide to the score

writing.selfCheckZh: 建議要針對新成員的具體參與障礙提出導入方法，保留舊成就但不讓它代替教學及聆聽；不聲稱一次介紹必定讓每人立即熟練。

takeaways.en: The festival could not live on reputation alone when returning visitors wanted to know how this year’s programme had been chosen.
takeaways.zh: 舊訪客想知道今年節目怎樣挑選時，藝術節不能只靠過去名聲維持。

takeaways.en: She warned that the workshop should not live on reputation alone and invited recent participants to describe the support they actually received.
takeaways.zh: 她提醒工作坊不應只靠過去名聲維持，並邀最近參與者描述實際得到的支援。

lessons.titleZh: 從雜訊中分辨真正資訊

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Editors help separate real information from noise.

brief.meaningEn: Distinguish useful, reliable information from distracting or unsupported messages.
brief.meaningZh: 把有用、可靠的資訊，與分散注意或未有支持的訊息分開。
brief.grammar: separate real information from noise; separated in past, separating in progress. Noise is figurative distraction or confusion, not necessarily a sound recording problem. Noise can also be accurate but irrelevant to a particular task; separating it concerns that task’s information needs, not automatically an accusation of falsehood.
brief.register: A conventional signal/noise comparison expressed in a productive separate-X-from-Y frame. A quiet message can be unreliable, and a widely repeated claim can remain unverified.
brief.boundaryZh: 要用來源及內容判斷，不只按聲量、轉發次數或自己喜不喜歡；少人說的主張也可能需要核對。 有些話可以真實，卻與目前要做的事無關；把它留在背景，不等於說它是假的。
brief.misconceptionZh: 分辨不等於只留下自己贊同的話，也不應把不確定意見寫成已確認決定。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出哪些內容已核實、哪些仍是提議或重複傳聞，並讓後續使用者看清分別。

listening.promptZh: 哪些內容已有依據？哪項仍未有來源？

options.en: A later start was confirmed in the dated update, while cancellation remained unsupported.
options.zh: 有日期的更新確認較遲開始，取消則仍未有支持。

options.en: Repeated screenshots were treated as enough confirmation that the event had been cancelled.
options.zh: 反覆轉傳的截圖，被當成活動已取消的充分確認。

options.en: The organiser confirmed that the original start time would remain unchanged.
options.zh: 主辦者確認，原定開始時間會保持不變。

options.en: The cancellation claim was traced to a named organiser before the check began.
options.zh: 核對開始前，取消說法已追溯到一位具名主辦者。

listening.explanationZh: 有依據的是開始時間較遲；不是原定時間照舊，重複截圖也不會自行為取消提供來源。
listening.en: We tried to separate real information from noise by checking the organiser’s dated update against the repeated screenshots; it confirmed a later start, while the claim about cancellation still had no named source.
listening.zh: 我們把主辦者有日期的更新，與反覆轉傳的截圖比較，嘗試從雜訊中分辨真正資訊；更新確認較遲開始，但取消的說法仍沒有具名來源。

reply.promptEn: Why did you compare the screenshots with the dated update?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼把截圖與有日期的更新比較？

options.en: We needed to separate real information from noise rather than count how often the claim appeared.
options.zh: 我們需要從雜訊中分辨真正資訊，而不是只數說法出現多少次。

options.en: The date and source could help us judge which timing information was current.
options.zh: 日期與來源，可幫我們判斷哪些時間資料是最新的。

options.en: The cancellation claim still lacked a named source.
options.zh: 取消的說法仍缺少具名來源。

options.en: Repetition alone did not establish what the organiser had actually changed.
options.zh: 重複本身不確立，主辦者實際改了甚麼。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出核對來源、日期及實際變更的目的，不以重複次數代替支持。

scene.promptZh: 小組錄音很清楚、背景安靜，但說話者只是猜測，沒有查過日期或來源。有人只因音質好，就說已從雜訊中分出真資訊。哪句最好？

options.en: Clear sound does not by itself separate real information from noise in this figurative sense; the claims still need checking.
options.zh: 在這個比喻用法中，聲音清楚本身不會分辨真正資訊與雜訊；主張仍需要核對。

options.en: The description concerns only the absence of background sound, so there is no need to consider the claims’ sources.
options.zh: 這個描述只關乎沒有背景聲，所以不需要考慮主張的來源。

options.en: The description says the speaker checked the date with the organiser before recording.
options.zh: 描述說，說話者錄音前已向主辦者核對日期。

scene.explanationZh: 這裏的比喻關乎訊息與來源，不只音質；安靜錄音也可錄下未核實猜測，不能因此不問來源。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 separate real information from noise 的查核目的？

options.en: Distinguish a confirmed change from an unsupported claim.
options.zh: 把已確認改動，與未有支持的主張分開。

options.en: Keep only the messages that support the conclusion one already prefers.
options.zh: 只保留支持自己原先偏好結論的訊息。

options.en: Check who supplied the information and whether it is current.
options.zh: 查看誰提供資訊，以及它是否仍適用。

contrast.explanationZh: 查核不是只挑合意訊息；應按來源及內容區分，而非先定結論。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「十個人轉同一圖，取消消息就可當定案吧？」你只找到主辦者確認改開始時間。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Let us separate real information from noise: the update confirms a later start, but the repeated image does not supply a source for cancellation.
options.zh: 我們先從雜訊中分辨真正資訊：更新確認較遲開始，但重複圖片沒有為取消提供來源。

options.en: I would use ten forwards as ten independent confirmations, even if they all show the same message.
options.zh: 即使都顯示同一訊息，我也會把十次轉傳當成十個獨立確認。

options.en: I would ignore the dated update because it is less widely shared than the screenshot.
options.zh: 我會忽略有日期的更新，因為它不如截圖傳得廣。

dialogue.explanationZh: 同一訊息重複傳送，不等於獨立來源；仍要看主辦者實際確認哪項改動。

speaking.en: To separate real information from noise, I want to know which details are confirmed and which are still suggestions or unsupported claims.
speaking.zh: 要從雜訊中分辨真正資訊，我想知道哪些細節已確認，哪些仍是建議或未有支持的主張。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再按確認狀態分辨資訊，而不是按聲量。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你協助朋友準備明天的編織工作坊。群組有真實但分散的舊活動回憶、茶點討論，以及最新材料清單；清單說每人帶毛線和針，織架由場地提供。你想請組長把收拾物品所需資訊置頂，保留其他聊天，不說那些回憶是假。用一至兩句英文提出實際整理請求。

examples.en: To separate real information from noise for tomorrow’s packing, could we pin a short list saying that we bring yarn and needles and the venue supplies the frames? The older stories and tea discussion can stay in the chat, but they do not answer what each person needs to carry.
examples.zh: 為準備明天要帶的東西，從雜訊中分辨所需資訊，我們可否置頂一張短清單，寫明我們帶毛線和針，織架由場地提供？舊故事及茶點討論可以留在群組，但沒有回答各人需要帶甚麼。

examples.en: Could we give the current materials list its own pinned note, showing what to bring and what the venue provides? That would help separate real information from noise for this task without treating the accurate but unrelated memories as false.
examples.zh: 我們可否把最新材料清單另設置頂便條，列明要帶甚麼，以及場地提供甚麼？這會幫助我們就這項任務，從雜訊中分辨所需資訊，而不把真實但無關的回憶當成假的。

writing.selfCheckZh: 請求要把帶物品這項任務需要的資訊清楚整理，保留其他聊天的位置；與目前任務無關，不等於內容不真實，也不用要求刪去所有回憶。

takeaways.en: She separated real information from noise in the interview notes by marking which times had been checked against the diary.
takeaways.zh: 她在訪問筆記中標出哪些時間已對照日記核實，藉此從雜訊中分辨真正資訊。

takeaways.en: The editor helped separate real information from noise, keeping the confirmed correction visible beside the remaining open questions.
takeaways.zh: 編輯幫忙從雜訊中分辨真正資訊，把已確認更正清楚放在仍待回答的問題旁。

lessons.titleEn: a cooler head in a very noisy world
lessons.titleZh: 在紛擾中提供較冷靜的判斷

target.pattern: \ba cooler head in a very noisy world\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Careful reporting provides a cooler head in a very noisy world.
sources.expression: a cooler head in a very noisy world

brief.meaningEn: A source of calmer judgement amid many competing reactions, claims or demands.
brief.meaningZh: 在許多互相爭持的反應、主張或要求之中，提供較冷靜判斷的人或事物。
brief.grammar: offer/provide/be a cooler head in a very noisy world. Cooler compares composure, not physical temperature; noisy can describe competing voices rather than actual volume.
brief.register: A creative combined image using conventional cool-head composure. Related to keeping a cool head, but this longer frame presents a calming contribution amid surrounding pressure, not a separate dictionary meaning.
brief.boundaryZh: 冷靜不等於漠不關心，也不是只看聲音大小；要指出怎樣協助釐清問題，而不替所有人作主。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能因某人說話慢就認定其判斷準確，也不把有情緒的人一概當成沒有相關經驗。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體聆聽、釐清或比較方式，說明冷靜判斷在紛擾中的作用。

listening.promptZh: 主席怎樣協助討論？她沒有把甚麼當成全體意見？

options.en: She asked about needs before comparing plans, rather than treating the loudest response as representative.
options.zh: 她先問需要，再比較方案，沒有把最響亮的回應當成代表。

options.en: She chose the loudest person’s plan before asking the other neighbours.
options.zh: 她還未問其他鄰居，就選了聲音最大那人的方案。

options.en: She refused to hear any concerns because a calm discussion should contain no disagreement.
options.zh: 她拒絕聽任何擔憂，因為冷靜討論不應包含分歧。

options.en: The chair compared which plan received the earliest reply rather than asking about the neighbours’ needs.
options.zh: 主席比較哪個方案最先收到回覆，而不是詢問鄰居的需要。

listening.explanationZh: 她先問需要，再比較方案，不是按聲量或回覆先後定案，也沒有排除不同擔憂。
listening.en: The chair offered a cooler head in a very noisy world by asking each neighbour what the garden needed before comparing the plans; she did not treat the loudest reaction as the whole group’s view.
listening.zh: 主席先問每位鄰居花園需要甚麼，再比較方案，在紛擾中提供了較冷靜的判斷；她沒有把最響亮的反應，當成全體意見。

reply.promptEn: Why did her contribution help the discussion?
reply.promptZh: 她的參與為甚麼有助討論？

options.en: She offered a cooler head in a very noisy world by making room for the needs behind the reactions.
options.zh: 她讓反應背後的需要有表達空間，在紛擾中提供較冷靜判斷。

options.en: The neighbours could explain what mattered before a plan was chosen.
options.zh: 選方案前，鄰居可以說明甚麼對自己重要。

options.en: The strongest reaction was not allowed to stand for everyone without further questions.
options.zh: 最強烈的反應，沒有在未追問下就代表所有人。

options.en: She gave the group a way to compare purposes rather than only react to one another.
options.zh: 她讓小組能比較目的，而不只是互相反應。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以具體討論方式作答；幫助不在於沒有分歧，而在於把不同需要說清楚。

scene.promptZh: 一位主持聲音很輕，卻未問其他人，就把第一位發言者的猜測當成定論。評語只因音量低便說他帶來較冷靜判斷。哪句最好？

options.en: A soft voice alone does not establish a cooler head in a very noisy world when the account shows no examination of the guess.
options.zh: 聲音輕本身，不確立他在紛擾中提供較冷靜判斷；敘述沒有顯示他檢視那個猜測。

options.en: The low volume confirms that he has compared the other participants’ needs.
options.zh: 音量低，確認他已比較其他參與者的需要。

options.en: The account describes him keeping the first claim open while asking for other evidence.
options.zh: 敘述描述他保留第一個主張未定，並詢問其他證據。

scene.explanationZh: 要看判斷及聆聽過程，不只聲音；這裏未檢視猜測就定案，不能補成已問過其他資料。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 a cooler head in a very noisy world 的判斷意象？

options.en: Make space to consider a concern before deciding.
options.zh: 決定前，留空間考慮一項擔憂。

options.en: Assume a calm manner gives someone the authority to decide what everyone needs without asking.
options.zh: 假定態度冷靜，就有權不問而決定每人需要甚麼。

options.en: Explain how the contribution helps people understand the disagreement.
options.zh: 解釋那份參與怎樣幫人理解分歧。

contrast.explanationZh: 冷靜可以幫助討論，不會自行賦予代所有人作主的權力。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「主席既然比較冷靜，就讓她不問大家而決定吧？」你重視她先聽需要的做法。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Being a cooler head in a very noisy world helps her guide the discussion, not replace the neighbours’ say in what matters to them.
options.zh: 在紛擾中提供較冷靜判斷，有助她引導討論，不是取代鄰居說明自身需要的權利。

options.en: I would take her calm tone as enough evidence that her first preference represents the whole street.
options.zh: 我會把她冷靜的語氣，當成她最初偏好已代表整條街的充分證據。

options.en: I would ask only the neighbours who can speak without showing any frustration.
options.zh: 我只會問那些能完全不表現挫折的鄰居。

dialogue.explanationZh: 判斷的幫助在於聽清及比較，不以冷靜語氣代替參與，也不只容納沒有情緒的人。

speaking.en: A patient question can offer a cooler head in a very noisy world without pretending that the disagreement does not matter.
speaking.zh: 耐心的一問，可以在紛擾中提供較冷靜判斷，而不假裝分歧不重要。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明耐心提問怎樣回應真正需要。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你收到三則互相牴觸的作品評語，現在難以決定先問哪條問題。你想請朋友陪你讀一次，幫忙找一個可行的下一步，不要求他替你決定整份作品。用一至兩句英文提出具體而有限的幫忙請求。

examples.en: I could use a cooler head in a very noisy world right now: could you read these three comments with me and help identify one question to ask next? I am not asking you to choose the whole project for me.
examples.zh: 現在我需要有人在紛擾中提供較冷靜判斷：你可否陪我讀這三則意見，幫忙找一條下一步可問的問題？我不是請你替我決定整份作品。

examples.en: Could you be a cooler head in a very noisy world for a moment and help me sort what these comments actually disagree about? I would like to choose my next question with a clearer picture, while keeping the work my own.
examples.zh: 你可否暫時在紛擾中提供較冷靜判斷，幫我整理這些意見實際在哪裏不同？我想看清楚一點，再選下一條問題，同時仍由自己作主完成作品。

glossary.zh: 保留自己對作品的主導

writing.selfCheckZh: 請求要指明可一起看的材料及有限下一步，不把支持變成代做整份作品；也不要求朋友抹去所有分歧。

takeaways.en: The librarian offered a cooler head in a very noisy world by separating the question about access from the argument about personal taste.
takeaways.zh: 圖書館員把使用機會的問題，與個人品味的爭論分開，在紛擾中提供較冷靜判斷。

takeaways.en: His short reflection became a cooler head in a very noisy world when it acknowledged the worry before asking what could be checked.
takeaways.zh: 他的短篇反思先承認擔心，再問哪些事情可核對，在紛擾中提供了較冷靜判斷。

lessons.titleZh: 讓這段關係持續有活力

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Video calls help keep that relationship alive.

brief.meaningEn: Maintain an active connection or bond between people rather than let it fade through lack of attention.
brief.meaningZh: 維持人與人之間仍有交流的連繫，而不任由關係因缺少關注而淡去。
brief.grammar: help keep that/our relationship alive; kept in past. The object is an interpersonal bond; alive describes continuing vitality rather than physical survival.
brief.register: Conventional keep-alive image with a relationship object. Related to sustaining interest in history, but this lesson practises ongoing reciprocal contact and care rather than preservation of historical knowledge.
brief.boundaryZh: 有聯絡方式不等於已維持有意義交流；不同人可商量不同頻率，不應把持續關係當成要求對方隨時回覆的權利。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能用訊息數量代替聆聽，也不把一種科技當成唯一維繫方法或成功保證。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體互相回應的方式說明維繫，也保留雙方實際意願及生活需要。

listening.promptZh: 關係怎樣得到維繫？通話是否唯一方式？

options.en: They responded to current interests through calls and letters, with more than one way to stay connected.
options.zh: 他們透過通話與書信回應當前興趣，有不只一種保持連繫的方式。

options.en: The calls replaced listening with a fixed list of questions that never referred to current life.
options.zh: 通話以固定問題清單代替聆聽，從不涉及當前生活。

options.en: They kept contact only by phone, and the letters were a plan they had not yet tried.
options.zh: 他們只靠電話保持聯絡，寫信則是尚未實行的計劃。

options.en: Their exchanges focused only on memories from before the move rather than current projects.
options.zh: 他們的交流只聚焦搬走前的回憶，沒有談當前正在做的事。

listening.explanationZh: 維繫來自持續互相回應，通話與書信可以互補，書信已是實際採用的另一方式，也不是只停在搬走前的回憶。
listening.en: Our monthly calls helped keep that relationship alive after my aunt moved: we asked about each other’s current projects, and later letters gave us another way to respond when a call was difficult.
listening.zh: 阿姨搬走後，每月通話幫忙維繫那段關係：我們問彼此正在做的事，之後寫信也讓難以通話時，有另一種回應方式。

reply.promptEn: What helped you remain connected after the move?
reply.promptZh: 搬走後，甚麼有助你們保持連繫？

options.en: The calls and later letters helped keep that relationship alive through interest in our current lives.
options.zh: 通話及之後書信，透過關心當前生活，幫忙維繫那段關係。

options.en: We asked about what each person was doing now.
options.zh: 我們問彼此現在正在做甚麼。

options.en: There was another way to respond when a call did not fit.
options.zh: 不方便通話時，還有另一種回應方式。

options.en: Both of us continued making room to hear and answer the other.
options.zh: 我們雙方都繼續留空間，聽取及回應對方。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出實際交流，而不是只看裝置、訊息次數或同住與否。

scene.promptZh: 人物每周自動寄出同一張問候卡，卻沒有看朋友回信提到的近況；他只按寄出次數，就說已充分維繫關係。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: The number of cards alone does not show how well they keep that relationship alive when the replies are not being heard.
options.zh: 沒有聽取回覆時，單憑卡片數量，不能顯示他們怎樣好好維繫那段關係。

options.en: Sending the repeated card establishes that he has responded to the friend’s latest concern.
options.zh: 寄出重複卡片，確立了他已回應朋友最新的擔憂。

options.en: The account says the two friends discussed the reply before choosing what to send next.
options.zh: 敘述說，兩人先討論回信，再選下一次寄甚麼。

scene.explanationZh: 寄出與回應近況不是同一件事；需要看有沒有聽見對方，而不只計次數。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 keep that relationship alive 的維繫意思？

options.en: Find an agreed way to hear what matters to one another now.
options.zh: 找雙方同意的方法，聽見彼此現在重視甚麼。

options.en: Treat the existence of a messaging account as proof that the bond is being maintained.
options.zh: 把一個通訊帳戶存在，當成關係已得到維繫的證明。

options.en: Allow different forms of contact when circumstances change.
options.zh: 情況改變時，容許不同聯絡形式。

contrast.explanationZh: 聯絡管道提供可能，實際維繫仍需要雙方的參與與回應。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「有每月通話，就把阿姨的信留着不讀也可以吧？」信提到她最近的新作品。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Calls can help keep that relationship alive, but I also want to read what she chose to share and answer her about it.
options.zh: 通話可以幫忙維繫那段關係，但我也想讀她選擇分享的事，並就此回應。

options.en: I would count the regular call as a response to the new letter without reading it.
options.zh: 我會把固定通話，當成對新信的回應，不用先讀。

options.en: I would replace her account of the new project with questions about the work she used to do.
options.zh: 我會用關於舊工作的問題，取代她對新作品的敘述。

dialogue.explanationZh: 形式可以互補，關鍵是回應她現在想分享的事，不讓固定習慣取代閱讀或了解新經歷。

speaking.en: I want to keep our relationship alive through attention to what matters to us now, not only by repeating how we used to talk.
speaking.zh: 我想透過關心雙方現在重視甚麼，讓關係持續有活力，而不只是重複以前的談話方式。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明怎樣回應目前的需要與興趣。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你因臨時取消已答應的探訪，令朋友失望；他說目前需要一點時間。你想為沒有及早通知道歉，表明珍惜關係，也會先歸還借來的書，不催促他立即原諒或回覆。用一至兩句英文寫實際訊息。

examples.en: I want to keep our relationship alive, but I know I let you down by cancelling without enough notice, and I am sorry. I will return the book as promised and give you the time you asked for, rather than ask for an immediate reply.
examples.zh: 我想讓我們的關係持續有活力，但知道沒有及早通知便取消，令你失望，對不起。我會按承諾歸還書，也給你所要求的時間，而不催你立即回覆。

examples.en: Keeping our relationship alive matters to me, and that includes taking your disappointment seriously. I am sorry I cancelled so late; I will return your book and leave you space before asking whether you want to arrange another visit.
examples.zh: 維繫我們的關係對我重要，這也包括認真對待你的失望。對不起，我太遲取消；我會歸還書，也先給你空間，之後才問是否想另約探訪。

writing.selfCheckZh: 訊息要為自己的具體行動道歉，實際履行歸還責任，也尊重對方要時間；不把想維繫當成要求立即原諒或回覆的理由。

takeaways.en: They kept their relationship alive by asking about the new routines rather than assuming the distance had changed nothing.
takeaways.zh: 他們詢問彼此的新作息，而不假定距離沒有帶來變化，藉此維繫關係。

takeaways.en: The shared sketchbook helped keep that relationship alive because each drawing invited a response from the other person.
takeaways.zh: 共用畫簿幫忙維繫那段關係，因為每幅畫都邀請對方回應。

lessons.titleZh: 持續掌握相關近況

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Group messages help residents stay in the loop.

brief.meaningEn: Remain informed about relevant developments or decisions in a group or activity.
brief.meaningZh: 持續知道小組或活動的相關進展或決定。
brief.grammar: stay in the loop about/on something; stayed in the loop. Being informed does not itself give authority to make every decision or require access to private information.
brief.register: Established information-membership idiom, not a physical loop. Identify the subject matter and the communication arrangement.
brief.boundaryZh: 知道近況與有權決定不同，也不表示必須即時讀每則訊息；範圍與方式可以商量。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能只因人在群組名單，就假定已收到或理解更新；也不要把所需更新擴成所有私密細節。
brief.outcomeZh: 能提出有範圍的資訊需要，並商量適合的更新方式。

listening.promptZh: 摘要讓說話者知道甚麼？是否要求他批准決定？

options.en: It explained confirmed and open matters without asking the reader to approve decisions.
options.zh: 它說明已確認及待議事項，沒有要求讀者批准決定。

options.en: It gave the absent member sole authority to decide every remaining question.
options.zh: 它給缺席成員單獨決定每條餘下問題的權力。

options.en: It confirmed that the reader had attended the meeting and voted on the room.
options.zh: 它確認，讀者已出席會議並就房間投票。

options.en: It contained only the old meeting agenda and no subsequent information.
options.zh: 它只有舊會議議程，沒有會後資訊。

listening.explanationZh: 摘要交代已定與未定事項，沒有要求缺席者批准；掌握近況也不等於曾在場投票，或已取得獨自決定權。
listening.en: Although I missed the planning meeting, the short summary helped me stay in the loop about the confirmed room and the questions still open; it did not ask me to approve decisions I had not discussed.
listening.zh: 雖然錯過規劃會議，簡短摘要幫我掌握已確認房間，以及仍待討論的問題；它沒有要我批准自己未討論過的決定。

reply.promptEn: Why was the summary useful after you missed the meeting?
reply.promptZh: 錯過會議後，摘要為甚麼有用？

options.en: It helped me stay in the loop about what was confirmed and what still needed discussion.
options.zh: 它幫我掌握哪些已確認，哪些仍需討論。

options.en: I could distinguish a settled arrangement from an open question.
options.zh: 我可以分清已定安排與待議問題。

options.en: I did not have to assume that every item on the original agenda had been decided.
options.zh: 我不用假定，原來議程每項都已定案。

options.en: The group’s current position was clearer even though I had not been there.
options.zh: 即使我不在場，小組目前的狀態也較清楚。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以會後資訊的用途作答，不把知道當成曾參與或已批准。

scene.promptZh: 成員只保存上月時間表，沒有讀最近更改日期的更新，卻說自己仍掌握最新安排。哪句最準確？

options.en: The old timetable alone does not show that the member has stayed in the loop about the recent change.
options.zh: 只保存舊時間表，不顯示成員已持續掌握最近改動。

options.en: Possessing last month’s timetable establishes knowledge of the newly changed date.
options.zh: 持有上月時間表，就確立知道新改日期。

options.en: The description says the member checked the change with the organiser before replying.
options.zh: 描述說，成員回覆前已向主辦者核對改動。

scene.explanationZh: 需要看有沒有得到相關新資訊，不能把舊文件的存在當作已知道新日期。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只從「I want to stay in the loop」推論出來？

options.en: The speaker wants relevant updates.
options.zh: 說話者想收到相關更新。

options.en: The speaker is claiming the right to control every decision.
options.zh: 說話者正在主張，有權控制每個決定。

options.en: The context can establish the scope of the information needed.
options.zh: 情境可以確定所需資訊的範圍。

contrast.explanationZh: 想掌握近況不等於要求控制；應按需要界定更新範圍。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「寄摘要給缺席者，就表示他已替我們批准房間吧？」你只想讓他知道進展。哪個回應最好？

options.en: The summary helps him stay in the loop; we should ask separately if we need his approval.
options.zh: 摘要幫他掌握近況；如果需要他的批准，應另行詢問。

options.en: I would treat receiving the summary as his vote for every item it mentions.
options.zh: 我會把收到摘要，當成他已對其中每項投贊成票。

options.en: I would assign him the unresolved questions simply because we have now briefed him.
options.zh: 我會只因現在已向他簡報，就把待議問題交給他負責。

dialogue.explanationZh: 通知、批准及接下責任是不同動作；需要同意便明確問，不把接收摘要當成投票或接受工作。

speaking.en: I would like to stay in the loop about the decisions that affect my role, without needing to read every informal message as it arrives.
speaking.zh: 我想掌握影響自己角色的決定，不必每則閒聊訊息一到就讀。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明想知道的範圍及適合的更新方式。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你接下來兩周要輪夜班，不能隨時看社團群組，但仍需要知道會改變你當值安排的決定。你想請聯絡人周五發一次重點摘要，緊急變更則另行短訊，不要求他轉發所有聊天。用一至兩句英文商量更新方式。

examples.en: I would like to stay in the loop about decisions affecting my shifts while I work nights. Could you send a brief Friday summary and text me separately about an urgent change, rather than forward every chat message?
examples.zh: 輪夜班期間，我想掌握影響當值的決定。你可否周五發一份重點摘要，緊急改動則另行短訊，而不轉發每則聊天？

examples.en: To stay in the loop without trying to follow the group all night, could I receive the key shift decisions each Friday? Please contact me separately if a change needs an answer before then.
examples.zh: 我想掌握近況，又不整晚追着群組看，可否每周五收到主要當值決定？如果某項改動需要在那之前答覆，請另行聯絡我。

writing.selfCheckZh: 回覆要給明確資訊範圍、固定摘要及例外聯絡方式，不把掌握近況等同接收所有聊天，也不承諾夜班期間隨時回覆。

takeaways.en: She stayed in the loop through the agreed weekly note, then asked a separate question before accepting a new responsibility.
takeaways.zh: 她透過議定的每周短報掌握近況，再另行詢問，才接受新責任。

takeaways.en: The coordinator helped volunteers stay in the loop by separating confirmed dates from suggestions still under discussion.
takeaways.zh: 統籌把已確認日期與仍待討論建議分開，幫義工掌握近況。

lessons.titleZh: 逐步消耗原可使用的時間

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Notifications eat away at hours of the day.
sources.expression: eat away at hours of the day

brief.meaningEn: Gradually reduce an available resource; in this lesson, small repeated demands consume time meant for something else.
brief.meaningZh: 逐漸減少可用資源；本課指反覆的小要求，消耗原本留給其他事情的時間。
brief.grammar: eat/eats/eating away at time; ate in past, has eaten in perfect. Keep away at before the object. The guide supplies hours of the day as a particular time object.
brief.register: Established phrasal verb of gradual erosion, used figuratively for time. Related eat into and chip away at have their own verb/particle forms; this is not a new meaning merely because the resource is time.
brief.boundaryZh: 重點在逐步累積，不是每次都很長，也不等於所有時間完全消失；需有反覆影響的具體資料。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要只憑一則必要提醒就說它必定耗去整天，也不把時間受到消耗當成已決定不再回應任何人。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述小要求怎樣累積耗時，並提出有範圍的調整方法。
brief.sourceClassificationNote: 原資料以 hours of the day 作時間受詞；本課練習可重用的 eat away at 片語動詞結構，描述時間逐步受到消耗。

listening.promptZh: 短查看怎樣累積影響閱讀？

options.en: The checks were short but repeated, with time lost returning to the text.
options.zh: 查看雖短卻反覆發生，也耗時重新回到文章。

options.en: One uninterrupted check took the entire half-hour before reading began.
options.zh: 開始閱讀前，一次未中斷的查看就用了整整半小時。

options.en: The alerts had been silenced, so the speaker read the full period without a break.
options.zh: 提醒已靜音，所以說話者整段時間都沒有中斷閱讀。

options.en: The speaker had deliberately scheduled a new task after each finished chapter.
options.zh: 說話者刻意在每章讀完後，安排一項新任務。

listening.explanationZh: 敘述強調短但反覆，以及重新找位置的累積消耗；不是單次查看或刻意按章安排任務。
listening.en: Repeated alerts were eating away at my reading time. Each check was brief, but finding my place again used up much of the half-hour I had set aside.
listening.zh: 反覆提醒正逐步消耗我的閱讀時間。每次查看都很短，但重新找回讀到哪裏，已用了預留半小時中的不少時間。

reply.promptEn: Why did the brief alerts matter to the reading period?
reply.promptZh: 短提醒為甚麼仍影響那段閱讀？

options.en: They were eating away at the time through repeated checks and restarts.
options.zh: 它們透過反覆查看及重新開始，逐步消耗時間。

options.en: A short interruption happened often enough to break up the planned half-hour.
options.zh: 短中斷發生得夠頻密，把計劃的半小時打散。

options.en: Returning to the text also took attention and time.
options.zh: 回到文章，也需要注意力及時間。

options.en: The effect depended on repetition, not only the length of a single check.
options.zh: 影響取決於反覆發生，不只看單次查看多長。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋短而多次的累積影響，不把每次簡短當成沒有代價。

scene.promptZh: 朋友在閱讀前先花兩分鐘回覆一則必要訊息，之後完整閱讀半小時，沒有再收到提醒。評論者只按有一則訊息，就說整段時間被反覆侵蝕。哪句最好？

options.en: This account does not yet show repeated interruptions eating away at the reading period; the message was handled before it began.
options.zh: 這段敘述還未顯示反覆中斷逐步消耗閱讀時段；訊息在開始前就已處理。

options.en: The single reply establishes that she repeatedly returned to messages during the reading.
options.zh: 一次回覆確立了，她在閱讀期間反覆回到訊息。

options.en: The description says the half-hour was stopped after each paragraph by another alert.
options.zh: 描述說，半小時閱讀在每段後，都被另一則提醒打斷。

scene.explanationZh: 要有累積消耗的資料；這裏分開處理必要訊息及完整閱讀，不是已描述反覆中斷。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只從「Small requests eat away at our time」推論出來？

options.en: The requests have a cumulative effect on available time.
options.zh: 要求對可用時間有累積影響。

options.en: Every individual request must take a long time by itself.
options.zh: 每一項要求本身都一定耗時很久。

options.en: Their frequency may help explain the loss of time.
options.zh: 頻率可能有助解釋時間消耗。

contrast.explanationZh: 逐步累積容許每次很短，不能把總影響當成每項本身都很長。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「每次問只要半分鐘，反覆打斷也不會影響閱讀吧？」你每次都要重新找位置。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Even short checks can eat away at the time when they keep making me restart; I would like a way to collect non-urgent questions.
options.zh: 如果不斷令我重新開始，短查看也可逐步消耗時間；我想找個方法，把非緊急問題集中起來。

options.en: I would judge the effect only by timing one reply, without counting how often I stop.
options.zh: 我只會計一次回覆多長，不數自己停下多少次。

options.en: I would add up only the typing time and ignore the effort of finding my place in the text again.
options.zh: 我只會把打字時間加起來，忽略重新找回讀到哪裏所花的工夫。

dialogue.explanationZh: 要同時看頻率與重新開始的成本，再商量集中處理的範圍；只計一次回覆或只計打字，都會漏掉部分影響。

speaking.en: Small requests can eat away at our time when they arrive one by one, so I want to discuss which can be gathered for a planned check.
speaking.zh: 小要求逐個到來時，可以逐步消耗我們的時間，所以我想商量哪些可集中到預定時段處理。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再交代累積方式與可調整的範圍。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們事後查看社團活動的準備記錄，發現多份核准表反覆要求相同資料，每次填寫只有幾分鐘，合起來卻侵佔準備時間；不是一次很長的延誤。你想向統籌提出流程檢視，先確認哪些核准真的必要，再刪減重複索取的資料，不直接取消所有核對。用一至兩句英文寫實際建議。

examples.en: The repeated approval forms ate away at our preparation period, even though no single delay was long. Could we review which approvals were necessary and remove duplicate requests for the same information?
examples.zh: 反覆的核准表逐步消耗我們的準備時段，即使沒有一次延誤很長。我們可否檢視哪些核准確實必要，再刪減重複索取相同資料的要求？

examples.en: Our log suggests that repeated requests for the same details were eating away at preparation time rather than causing one large delay. Let us trace which checks actually served a purpose before simplifying the forms, so we retain the safeguards we still need.
examples.zh: 記錄顯示，反覆索取相同細節，正逐步消耗準備時間，而不是造成一次長延誤。我們先查清哪些核對確實有作用，再簡化表格，保留仍需要的保障。

writing.selfCheckZh: 建議要按記錄指出逐次累積的耗時，提出檢視必要性及減少重複資料的步驟；不把問題誤成一次長延誤，也不未查作用就取消所有核對。

takeaways.en: Last-minute revisions ate away at the afternoon reserved for recording, so the team agreed which changes could wait.
takeaways.zh: 臨時修改逐步消耗預留錄音的下午，所以小組議定哪些改動可以等。

takeaways.en: The extra forms had eaten away at her preparation period before she realised how many separate approvals were being requested.
takeaways.zh: 她發現原來需要多少項分開批准前，額外表格已逐步消耗她的準備時段。
