lessons.titleZh: 沒有自然停點的持續滑動內容

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The endless scroll can consume an evening.

brief.meaningEn: A continuous feed experience in which more content keeps appearing without an obvious natural stopping point.
brief.meaningZh: 更多內容持續出現、沒有明顯自然停點的動態閱讀經驗。
brief.grammar: the endless scroll; get caught in/return to the endless scroll. Endless describes the experience of continuing content, not a literal mathematical assertion that the system contains infinitely many items.
brief.register: A transparent digital-content noun phrase, not an opaque idiom. It describes a pattern of consumption; the context establishes whether it distracts or serves a chosen purpose.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是每次在螢幕上向下移動，都叫沒有停點的持續內容；要看是否有清楚結尾及當事人原來的目的。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能只按滑動動作就診斷一個人，也不把有限相簿、長文章與不斷接續的動態一概混同。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述內容怎樣缺少停點，並提出與實際閱讀目的相符的選擇。

listening.promptZh: 原來目的與後來的閱讀經驗，有甚麼差別？

options.en: The speaker wanted one photograph but continued through a feed without a clear stopping point.
options.zh: 說話者本想找一張照片，卻在沒有清楚停點的動態中繼續看下去。

options.en: The speaker read a fixed twelve-photo album and stopped at its labelled final page.
options.zh: 說話者讀完固定十二張照片的相簿，在標明的最後一頁停下。

options.en: The feed showed only the requested caption, with no other posts appearing.
options.zh: 動態只顯示所需圖說，沒有其他貼文出現。

options.en: The speaker closed the feed immediately after confirming the original caption.
options.zh: 說話者核對原先圖說後，就立即關上動態。

listening.explanationZh: 敘述對比原來的單一目的與持續接續內容，最後也沒有完成想查的圖說；不是明確讀完有限相簿。
listening.en: I opened the feed to find one exhibition photo, then got caught in the endless scroll as more posts followed without a clear finish; by the time I closed it, I had forgotten which caption I wanted to check.
listening.zh: 我打開動態，本想找一張展覽照片，卻在貼文不斷接續、沒有清楚結尾時，陷進持續滑動的內容；關上時，已忘了原本想核對哪則圖說。

reply.promptEn: Why did you lose track of the caption you meant to check?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼忘了原本想核對的圖說？

options.en: I got caught in the endless scroll as more posts kept following.
options.zh: 更多貼文不斷接續，令我陷進沒有自然停點的持續內容。

options.en: The feed kept offering another item instead of a clear finish to the search.
options.zh: 動態不斷給下一項內容，而沒有讓搜尋清楚結束。

options.en: My attention moved from one exhibition photo to the following posts.
options.zh: 我的注意力從一張展覽照片，移到其後貼文。

options.en: I continued browsing after losing sight of the original purpose.
options.zh: 我忘了原來目的後，仍繼續瀏覽。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述注意力及內容接續的過程，不把單純滑動或任何長文章一概當成相同情況。

scene.promptZh: 相簿有十二張照片、清楚編號，最後標明「完」。人物按計劃看完便關上，只因有向下移動，就有人稱這是不斷延伸的動態。哪句最好？

options.en: A finite album with a clear ending is not by itself the endless scroll described by the feed image.
options.zh: 有清楚結尾的有限相簿，本身不等於動態意象中沒有自然停點的持續內容。

options.en: Moving down the page establishes that more items kept appearing after the labelled ending.
options.zh: 向下移動頁面，確立了標明結尾後仍有更多項目不斷出現。

options.en: The account says the person abandoned the twelve photographs to follow an unrelated feed.
options.zh: 敘述說，人物放下十二張照片，轉而跟看沒有關聯的動態。

scene.explanationZh: 要看內容的接續及結尾；這裏是有數量及完成標示的相簿，不是只因滑動就沒有停點。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只從「I got caught in the endless scroll」推論出來？

options.en: The speaker experienced a continuing feed without an obvious stopping point.
options.zh: 說話者經歷了沒有明顯停點的持續動態。

options.en: The phrase proves that continuing through the feed was the speaker’s original plan.
options.zh: 這句話證明，持續瀏覽動態原本就是說話者的計劃。

options.en: More context can show what the speaker originally meant to do.
options.zh: 更多情境可以說明，說話者原先想做甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 這個描述交代閱讀經驗，本身不證明原本就打算一直看；需要更多情境理解原來目的。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「只要手指向下滑，就一定是那種停不了的動態吧？」你想區分有限相簿與不斷接續內容。哪個回應最好？

options.en: The endless scroll concerns how content keeps continuing; a twelve-photo album with an end can involve the same finger movement.
options.zh: 沒有自然停點的持續內容，關乎內容怎樣接續；有結尾的十二張相簿，也可以用同樣手指動作。

options.en: I would classify the album only by whether a finger moves down the screen.
options.zh: 我只會按手指有沒有向下移動螢幕，把相簿分類。

options.en: I would also call a long article the endless scroll on length alone, even if the text has a fixed conclusion.
options.zh: 我也會只按篇幅，把一篇有明確結尾的長文章稱為同樣沒有停點的持續內容。

dialogue.explanationZh: 動作或篇幅不等於內容結構；要看是否有選定範圍、固定內容及真正結尾。

speaking.en: I want to find the caption I came for, rather than lose it in the endless scroll of posts that keep leading somewhere else.
speaking.zh: 我想找到原本要看的圖說，而不在不斷把我帶向別處的持續貼文中，把目的忘掉。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說清原來目的與內容接續的差別。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替小型博物館策劃線上相簿，目的是讓訪客看懂一位木匠的三個製作步驟。你想先提供有清楚結尾的選定照片與圖說，完整資料庫另設連結，避免作品流程被沒有停點的其他圖片淹沒。用一至兩句英文向同伴提出策劃安排。

examples.en: Let’s give the three stages a clear beginning and ending, rather than lose the process in the endless scroll. We can offer a separate archive link after the selected photographs and captions for visitors who want more.
examples.zh: 我們讓三個階段有清楚開始與結尾，不讓製作過程淹沒在沒有自然停點的持續內容中。選定照片及圖說之後，可以另提供資料庫連結，給想看更多的訪客。

examples.en: I would keep the carpenter’s sequence separate from the endless scroll of other images. A finite set of captioned photographs can explain the process, with the full archive available by choice afterwards.
examples.zh: 我會把木匠的製作次序，與其他圖片沒有停點的持續內容分開。一組數量有限、附圖說的照片，可以解釋過程；之後想看的人，再自行選擇完整資料庫。

writing.selfCheckZh: 安排要支援理解製作步驟，讓選定範圍有清楚結尾，也保留自選深入資料；不只要求完全停止用螢幕，也不把其他圖片一概當成無價值。

takeaways.en: The endless scroll made it hard for him to find the one dated notice he had opened the page to read.
takeaways.zh: 沒有自然停點的持續內容，令他難以找到原本打開頁面要讀的那則有日期通知。

takeaways.en: She left the endless scroll for a captioned album with a final page, choosing to finish the family sequence before browsing anything else.
takeaways.zh: 她離開沒有自然停點的持續內容，改看附圖說及最後一頁的相簿，選擇先看完整段家人照片，再瀏覽其他內容。

lessons.titleZh: 只挑選亮眼時刻呈現的片段

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Do not compare real life with highlight reels.

brief.meaningEn: Selected displays of especially positive or striking moments, used figuratively for a curated public picture of life.
brief.meaningZh: 挑選特別正面或亮眼時刻呈現的內容；比喻經挑選、讓公眾看見的生活樣貌。
brief.grammar: a highlight reel / highlight reels; compare an ordinary day with someone’s highlight reel. In the social comparison use, the images can be real while remaining selective.
brief.register: A media term extended from compilations of notable footage to curated personal displays. It does not inherently accuse the maker of fabrication.
brief.boundaryZh: 片段可真實卻不完整；看不到困難，不表示那些困難不存在，也不表示每位分享者一定過得很差。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能把自己的完整日常跟別人的精選時刻當成同等資料比較，也不應要求別人公開所有私事來證明真實。
brief.outcomeZh: 能承認分享的喜悅，同時說清選取範圍與仍未知的生活部分。

listening.promptZh: 真實照片與完整記錄，有甚麼分別？

options.en: The images were real but selective, leaving out other parts of the week.
options.zh: 照片真實卻經過挑選，沒有呈現那周的其他部分。

options.en: The photographs had been established as staged copies from a different workshop.
options.zh: 照片已被證實是另一工作坊擺拍的複製品。

options.en: The posts documented the repairs and disagreements in the same detail as the finished work.
options.zh: 帖文跟成品一樣詳細記錄了修補及分歧。

options.en: The finished pieces were absent, and the feed concerned only problems before the workshop began.
options.zh: 成品沒有出現，動態只關乎工作坊開始前的問題。

listening.explanationZh: 精選可以使用真實內容，但沒有代表每個經過；未展示的修補與分歧，也不等於照片造假。
listening.en: Their posts were highlight reels of the workshop: smiling portraits and the finished pieces were real, but the late repairs and quiet disagreements were not shown, so the feed was not a complete record of the week.
listening.zh: 他們的帖文是工作坊的精選時刻：微笑肖像與成品都真實，但較後的修補及安靜分歧沒有出現，所以動態不是整周的完整記錄。

reply.promptEn: Why did you not treat the posts as a full account of the week?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼沒有把帖文當成整周完整敘述？

options.en: They were highlight reels, showing selected moments rather than everything that happened.
options.zh: 它們是精選時刻，展示經挑選的片段，而不是發生過的一切。

options.en: The late repairs and quiet disagreements were missing.
options.zh: 較後的修補及安靜分歧沒有出現。

options.en: The photographs showed the finished work without the whole process behind it.
options.zh: 照片展示成品，沒有它背後的全部過程。

options.en: A real image could still represent only one part of the experience.
options.zh: 真實照片仍可能只代表經驗的一部分。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都按選取範圍解釋，不把真實與完整混為一談，也不無據指控造假。

scene.promptZh: 一位朋友只分享畢業當天最開心的兩張照片，沒有聲稱每天都同樣開心。另一人由此斷定他從來沒有遇過困難。哪句最好？

options.en: Those pictures may be part of his highlight reel, but they do not establish what every other day was like.
options.zh: 那些照片可能是他精選時刻的一部分，但不確立其他每一天怎樣。

options.en: The two pictures establish that he found every stage of the course equally easy.
options.zh: 兩張照片確立了，他覺得課程每個階段都同樣容易。

options.en: Sharing a happy moment is itself a claim that the entire course contained no difficulty.
options.zh: 分享開心時刻，本身就是聲稱整個課程沒有困難。

scene.explanationZh: 分享局部喜悅不等於對所有日子下結論；應保留照片實際呈現的範圍。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 highlight reels 的社群生活比喻？

options.en: Recognise that the selection may leave out ordinary or difficult moments.
options.zh: 承認挑選可能沒有包括平常或困難時刻。

options.en: Treat the selective display as proof that every pictured achievement was fabricated.
options.zh: 把經挑選的展示，當成照片裏每項成就都造假的證明。

options.en: Allow someone to celebrate without assuming the display is a complete life record.
options.zh: 容許一個人慶祝，同時不假定展示是完整人生記錄。

contrast.explanationZh: 經挑選與造假不同；需要另有證據，才能判斷某項內容是否不真實。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「沒拍修補過程，就證明成品照片是假的吧？」照片來自真實作品。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Highlight reels can leave work out without inventing the finished piece; I would ask about the process rather than assume the image is false.
options.zh: 精選時刻可以漏去部分工作，卻沒有編造成品；我會問過程，而不先假定照片是假的。

options.en: I thought posting only the finished piece meant the maker was claiming there had been no repairs.
options.zh: 我原以為，只貼成品，就表示製作者在聲稱沒有做過修補。

options.en: I would take the real finished image as enough to conclude that the whole workshop went smoothly.
options.zh: 我會把真實成品照片，當成整個工作坊都順利的充分依據。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可以承認作品真實，也仍缺部分過程；只分享成品，不會自動聲稱沒有修補，也不證明全程順利。

speaking.en: A highlight reel can show something genuinely joyful without showing what every ordinary day involved.
speaking.zh: 精選時刻可以展示真正開心的事，而不展示每個平常日子包含甚麼。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再區分真實喜悅、選取範圍與完整生活。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你要替自己完成木凳的照片寫貼文。你真心高興成品，也想承認照片只是一段亮眼時刻，並簡短提到重做接合處；你不想為證明真實而公開所有私人煩惱。用一至兩句英文寫實際圖說。

examples.en: These photographs are part of my highlight reel, and I am genuinely happy to have finished the stool. The joints took another attempt; this is a moment I want to celebrate, not a record of everything else in my week.
examples.zh: 這些照片是我精選時刻的一部分，我也真心高興完成木凳。接合處曾重做一次；這是我想慶祝的片刻，不是那周其他所有事情的記錄。

examples.en: Here is one piece of my highlight reel: a finished stool after reworking the joints. I am pleased with this part of the process, while keeping the rest of the week my own.
examples.zh: 這是我精選時刻的一小部分：重做接合處後完成的木凳。我對過程這一部分感到高興，同時保留那周其餘事情的私人空間。

glossary.en: a moment I want to celebrate

writing.selfCheckZh: 圖說要有真實喜悅及可自選的具體過程，說清只是部分經歷；不用抹去成果，也不用公開全部私事。

takeaways.en: Her travel photographs formed a highlight reel, so he asked what the ordinary working days had been like before comparing their experiences.
takeaways.zh: 她的旅遊照片形成精選時刻，所以比較彼此經歷前，他先問平常工作日怎樣。

takeaways.en: The class shared a highlight reel of the performance and kept a separate record of the changes they wanted to discuss later.
takeaways.zh: 班級分享演出的精選片段，也另記下之後想討論的改動。

lessons.titleZh: 把人拉離原來目標

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Late-night feeds can pull people off track.

brief.meaningEn: Distract people from the goal or direction they were trying to follow.
brief.meaningZh: 使人分心，偏離原本想跟隨的目標或方向。
brief.grammar: pull someone off track; pulled/pulling; name the intended goal and how attention shifts away. A relevant change of task need not be a distraction.
brief.register: Conventional path-and-direction metaphor, not a literal railway claim. Off track concerns a relationship to purpose, not a judgement that the distracting topic has no value anywhere.
brief.boundaryZh: 要先知道目標，才判斷是否偏離；有用的核對也可能暫時改變動作，不應只按停頓或興趣判斷。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能把所有新問題都視為干擾，也不能把偏離某項任務，說成那個人或話題完全沒有價值。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出偏離的具體方式，並有禮提出返回任務或另留時間的方法。

listening.promptZh: 原本目標與實際結果，有甚麼差別？

options.en: They spent the session on poster choices instead of preparing the interview opening.
options.zh: 他們把那一節用在海報選擇，沒有準備訪問開場。

options.en: The poster comparison was the agreed purpose of the session, and the interview had already been completed.
options.zh: 比較海報是那一節已議定的目的，訪問也已完成。

options.en: They finished the interview questions before briefly checking a colour.
options.zh: 他們先完成訪問問題，之後才簡短查看一種顏色。

options.en: The guest had asked them to replace all interview questions with a poster.
options.zh: 來賓已要求他們以海報取代所有訪問問題。

listening.explanationZh: 偏離是相對於準備訪問問題的目標；選色有結果，卻沒有完成原先需要的開場問題。
listening.en: Comparing unrelated poster styles pulled us off track while we were meant to prepare interview questions; by the end of the session, we had chosen colours but still had no opening question for the guest.
listening.zh: 我們本應準備訪問問題，卻因比較沒有關聯的海報風格而偏離目標；那一節結束時，選好了顏色，仍沒有給來賓的開場問題。

reply.promptEn: Why did you say the comparison distracted the group?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼說那場比較令小組分心？

options.en: It pulled us off track from preparing the questions we needed for the guest.
options.zh: 它把我們拉離了為來賓準備問題的目標。

options.en: We ended with colours rather than an interview opening.
options.zh: 我們最後有了顏色，卻沒有訪問開場。

options.en: The activity did not serve the task we had agreed for that session.
options.zh: 那個活動沒有支援這一節已議定的工作。

options.en: We spent the available attention on something unrelated to the planned questions.
options.zh: 我們把可用的注意力，花在與計劃問題無關的事情。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都按目標及結果說明偏離，不把海報設計本身一概說成沒有價值。

scene.promptZh: 研究者暫停寫段落，先核對一個會影響論點的日期，再回去修正原句；朋友只因她停筆，就說她偏離工作。哪句最準確？

options.en: A relevant check does not necessarily pull her off track; it can support the argument she is working on.
options.zh: 相關核對不一定把她拉離目標，也可支援正在處理的論點。

options.en: Checking the date shows she has chosen a new research question rather than refining the existing argument.
options.zh: 核對日期顯示，她已選一條新研究問題，而不是改進現有論點。

options.en: The date check concerned an unrelated event-planning task rather than the argument.
options.zh: 日期核對關乎無關的活動規劃工作，而不是那個論點。

scene.explanationZh: 核對與原論點有關，不能只按動作改變就判偏離，也沒有說放棄了原工作。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 pull people off track 的任務比喻？

options.en: Identify the goal that attention has moved away from.
options.zh: 指出注意力離開了哪個目標。

options.en: Assume the distracting topic has no value for any other purpose.
options.zh: 假定那個令人分心的話題，對其他任何目的都沒有價值。

options.en: Explain why a different activity does or does not serve the current task.
options.zh: 解釋另一活動是否支援目前工作。

contrast.explanationZh: 偏離當前目標與完全沒有價值不同；同一話題可在別的目的下有用。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「既然選好顏色，就當訪問準備完成吧？」你們仍未有開場問題。哪個回應最好？

options.en: The poster work pulled us off track from the interview; I would return to the opening question before calling the preparation complete.
options.zh: 海報工作把我們拉離訪問目標；說準備完成前，我會先回到開場問題。

options.en: I would call the preparation finished because we completed the part that was easiest to agree on.
options.zh: 我會因最容易達成共識的部分已完成，就說準備已做好。

options.en: I would spend the remaining session refining the poster and leave question drafting until the guest arrives.
options.zh: 我會把餘下時段用來改善海報，等來賓到達才起草問題。

dialogue.explanationZh: 其他工作有進展，不會代替尚未做的訪問準備；要回到目標所需的具體內容。

speaking.en: A useful question can change what I do next without pulling me off track, if it helps the purpose we agreed to pursue.
speaking.zh: 有用的問題可以改變我下一步做甚麼，而不使我偏離目標，只要它支援我們議定的目的。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再用目的判斷改變與偏離。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你請同伴討論小說的敘述視角，他卻一直猜故事是否在影射你的家人。你不想公開私事，仍願意聽他就文本說哪些地方難懂。用一至兩句英文有禮說明界線，請回到可討論的作品問題。

examples.en: Guessing about my family is pulling us off track from the viewpoint question I wanted help with. Could we stay with what the narrator says on the page, while leaving my private life out of this discussion?
examples.zh: 猜測我的家人，把我們拉離了我想請你幫忙的視角問題。我們可否留在頁面上敘述者實際說的內容，把我的私生活留在這場討論之外？

examples.en: I am happy to hear where the story is unclear, but speculation about my relatives pulls us off track. Please show me the passage that confused you so we can discuss how the viewpoint works.
examples.zh: 我願意聽故事哪裏不清楚，但猜測我的親人，讓我們偏離目標。請指出令你困惑的段落，讓我們討論視角怎樣運作。

writing.selfCheckZh: 回覆要提出文本討論的具體方向，也清楚保留私人界線；不因拒絕傳記猜測，就把同伴對作品的所有問題排除。

takeaways.en: The debate over the cover pulled them off track from checking the permissions that had to be settled before printing.
takeaways.zh: 封面的爭論把他們拉離了核對許可的目標，而那些許可必須在印刷前落實。

takeaways.en: She asked whether the new example helped the central question or was pulling the class off track towards a different topic.
takeaways.zh: 她問新例子有助核心問題，還是把全班拉向另一話題、偏離目標。

lessons.titleZh: 離開應用程式，暫停使用

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: He will come off the app after reading the group updates.

brief.meaningEn: Stop using or engaging with an app or platform for a period specified by the context.
brief.meaningZh: 在情境所說的時段，停止使用或參與某個應用程式或平台。
brief.grammar: come off the app/social media; came/coming off. State the period if known. The source uses leaving an app after reading updates; the phrase does not itself require account deletion.
brief.register: A contextual platform-use extension, especially found in British discussion of coming off social media. Other come-off senses include detachment and success; those are not taught here.
brief.boundaryZh: 暫停多久、是否刪帳戶或仍需其他聯絡方式，都要按上下文；不能只由 come off 補成永久離開或完成刪除。
brief.misconceptionZh: 離開一個平台不表示不在乎其中的人；也不能把關閉畫面當成已回覆所有未完成事情。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說清暫停的範圍、期間，以及需要另行交代的事項。

listening.promptZh: 這次停止使用，有甚麼範圍與後續安排？

options.en: The speaker plans to stop after one update and use the agreed email route for a later question.
options.zh: 說話者計劃讀完一則更新便停止，之後的問題則用議定電郵途徑。

options.en: The speaker has promised to answer every group message before leaving tonight.
options.zh: 說話者已承諾今晚離開前，回答群組每則訊息。

options.en: The group and account will be permanently deleted after the update.
options.zh: 讀完更新後，群組及帳戶會永久刪除。

options.en: The speaker will ignore the rehearsal update and send no question by any route.
options.zh: 說話者會忽略排練更新，也不以任何途徑發問。

listening.explanationZh: 這裏交代今晚的停止點及後續電郵，不等於刪帳戶、全部回覆或完全不聯絡。
listening.en: I will come off the app after reading the rehearsal update tonight, then leave tomorrow’s question for our agreed email exchange; I am not deleting the group or promising to answer every message before I stop.
listening.zh: 今晚讀完排練更新後，我會離開應用程式，明天的問題則留到議定的電郵交流；我不是刪除群組，也不是承諾停用前回答每則訊息。

reply.promptEn: What are you planning to do after reading tonight’s update?
reply.promptZh: 讀完今晚更新後，你打算做甚麼？

options.en: I will come off the app and use our agreed email exchange for tomorrow’s question.
options.zh: 我會離開應用程式，明天的問題則用議定電郵交流。

options.en: I will stop using the app for the evening rather than try to clear every message.
options.zh: 我會在當晚停止使用，而不是嘗試清完每則訊息。

options.en: The later question can wait for the communication route we have already agreed.
options.zh: 之後的問題，可以留到我們已議定的聯絡途徑。

options.en: I intend to finish reading the update, then leave the app for now.
options.zh: 我打算先讀完更新，再暫時離開應用程式。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都符合已說明的停止與後續安排，不加入永久刪除或所有訊息已處理的主張。

scene.promptZh: 人物只把群組設為靜音，仍一直打開應用程式閱讀和回覆；她沒有說自己已停止使用。旁人把靜音當成已離開。哪句最好？

options.en: Muting alerts does not by itself mean she has come off the app when she is still actively using it.
options.zh: 她仍在主動使用時，提醒靜音本身不表示她已離開應用程式。

options.en: Turning off the sound establishes that she has stopped reading and replying.
options.zh: 關閉聲音，確立了她已停止閱讀及回覆。

options.en: The account says she deleted the app before reading the group messages.
options.zh: 敘述說，她在讀群組訊息前，就刪除了應用程式。

scene.explanationZh: 提醒聲與使用行為不同；要看是否停止參與，而不只看聲音設定。

contrast.promptZh: 在今晚暫停使用的情境中，哪項最不能只從「I will come off the app」得出？

options.en: The speaker plans to stop engaging with the app.
options.zh: 說話者計劃停止使用應用程式。

options.en: The speaker has necessarily deleted the account permanently.
options.zh: 說話者必定已永久刪除帳戶。

options.en: More context can specify when the pause ends.
options.zh: 更多情境可以說明，暫停何時結束。

contrast.explanationZh: 停止使用的時間與帳戶是否刪除，是不同資料；片語本身不完成刪除動作。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「你今晚要停用，就代表我明天的問題不能再問了吧？」你們已約好用電郵。哪個回應最好？

options.en: I will come off the app tonight, but I still want your question through the email arrangement we agreed.
options.zh: 我今晚會離開應用程式，但仍想按已議定的電郵安排，收到你的問題。

options.en: I would treat leaving one app as cancelling our agreement to discuss the question by email.
options.zh: 我會把離開一個應用程式，當成取消電郵討論問題的約定。

options.en: I thought tomorrow’s question had already been answered by tonight’s update, so I would not expect a separate email.
options.zh: 我原以為，明天的問題已由今晚更新回答，所以不會預期另有電郵。

dialogue.explanationZh: 平台與仍在的溝通承諾需要分開；今晚更新沒有被描述為已回答之後的問題，停止使用也不會取消另一途徑。

speaking.en: I am going to come off the app for the evening, but I will be clear about which messages can wait and how to reach me for the agreed task.
speaking.zh: 今晚我打算離開應用程式，但會說清哪些訊息可等，以及議定工作應怎樣聯絡我。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明暫停使用與仍需履行的溝通安排。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你訪問一位創作者，他說自己曾停用一個社群平台六周，仍透過網站接受作品查詢。稿件卻寫成「退出創作、不再與任何人聯絡」。你想向編輯更正範圍，不聲稱那六周使用所有平台的情況都已知道。用一至兩句英文提出修改。

examples.en: He said he had come off the platform for six weeks, not that he had stopped making work or receiving enquiries through his website. Could we keep those limits clear instead of describing a complete withdrawal?
examples.zh: 他說的是停用那個平台六周，不是停止創作或停止透過網站接受查詢。我們可否說清這些範圍，而不寫成完全退出？

examples.en: Coming off social media in his account referred to that platform and that six-week period. Please retain the separate website contact rather than imply he ended every professional connection.
examples.zh: 他敘述中的停用社群媒體，指那個平台及那六周。請保留另有網站聯絡方式，不暗示他結束了每段專業連繫。

writing.selfCheckZh: 修改要保留平台、時段及另有查詢途徑的範圍；不把停用一處擴成退出創作，也不補上其他平台的未知情況。

takeaways.en: She came off the platform for a month and told her collaborators which email address she would check instead.
takeaways.zh: 她停用那個平台一個月，並告訴合作伙伴會改看哪個電郵地址。

takeaways.en: He planned to come off the app after sending the agreed note, without treating that pause as a decision to leave the choir.
takeaways.zh: 他計劃傳送議定短箋後便離開應用程式，沒有把暫停當成退出合唱團的決定。

english.evidence: BBC primary reports attest coming off social media for a specified period; no claim that dictionary app-specific stop-use sense is universal. Exact guide app source retained, separating cessation from account deletion. Final actual profile correction concerns professional withdrawal scope rather than another personal evening-stop plan.

lessons.titleEn: take to it like a duck to water
lessons.titleZh: 初次接觸便輕鬆上手

target.pattern: \b(?:take(?:s)?|took|taken|taking) to (?:it|this|the task) like a duck to water\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Given a small keyboard, many children take to it like a duck to water.
sources.expression: take to it like a duck to water

brief.meaningEn: Begin doing something with apparent natural ease or enjoyment, especially on first trying it.
brief.meaningZh: 初次嘗試某事時，便顯得自然輕鬆或樂在其中。
brief.grammar: take to it like a duck to water; took/taken/taking. It refers to an activity established by context. Easy initial adaptation does not establish mastery of every related task.
brief.register: An established ease-and-adaptation idiom. It describes the observed person and activity, not a rule about what all children or beginners can do.
brief.boundaryZh: 初步上手容易，與已掌握所有相關知識不同；之後的熟練表現，也不能單憑結果證明初次便輕鬆。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要因自己很快學會，就假定別人需要相同節奏，或把需要多練習的人說成沒有能力。
brief.outcomeZh: 能形容初次學習的順利，同時保留仍須學習的範圍，並配合別人的步伐。

listening.promptZh: 輕鬆上手的是甚麼？哪項問題仍需學習？

options.en: Jin learned the basic controls easily but still needed guidance about permission to publish.
options.zh: Jin 輕鬆學會基本控制，但仍需指導，了解公開錄音的許可。

options.en: Jin had already obtained permission from the recorded speaker before learning the controls.
options.zh: Jin 學習控制操作前，已取得錄音中說話者的許可。

options.en: The account describes a long struggle with the basic controls followed by eventual success.
options.zh: 敘述描述了 Jin 長期難以掌握基本控制，最後才成功。

options.en: The tutor was teaching permission rules rather than demonstrating any recording controls.
options.zh: 導師當時在教許可規則，沒有示範任何錄音控制。

listening.explanationZh: 這個慣用語形容初步操作的自然順利；Jin 仍提出許可問題，不是已掌握公開錄音的一切要求。
listening.en: Jin took to it like a duck to water when shown the basic recording controls, but still asked how to obtain permission before publishing another person’s voice; easy controls did not settle that separate question.
listening.zh: Jin 初次學習基本錄音控制便輕鬆上手，但仍詢問公開別人的聲音前，應怎樣取得許可；控制操作容易，並沒有解決那個另一層面的問題。

reply.promptEn: Why did you describe Jin as a quick beginner with the recorder?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼說 Jin 初學錄音機時上手很快？

options.en: Jin took to it like a duck to water when trying the basic controls.
options.zh: Jin 嘗試基本控制時，便輕鬆上手。

options.en: The basic operation seemed easy from the first demonstration.
options.zh: 從第一次示範起，基本操作便顯得容易。

options.en: There was little difficulty starting the task, although permission was a separate question.
options.zh: 開始操作時沒有甚麼困難，但許可仍是另一個問題。

options.en: Jin quickly became comfortable using the controls that had just been shown.
options.zh: Jin 很快便能自在使用剛示範過的控制。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以初次操作的順利解釋上手快；沒有把容易操作擴成已取得許可或完全專業。

scene.promptZh: 一位演奏者說，剛學這首曲時節拍很難，多月練習後才自在演出。朋友只看最後演出，便說她初次便自然上手。哪句最好？

options.en: Her fluent performance does not establish that she took to it like a duck to water; her account describes a difficult beginning and later practice.
options.zh: 她流暢的演出，不能確立她初次便輕鬆上手；她的敘述是開始時困難，之後經過練習。

options.en: The final performance establishes that the first attempt felt equally easy.
options.zh: 最後的演出確立了，第一次嘗試時也同樣容易。

options.en: The practice was needed only for performing in public, not for learning the difficult rhythm.
options.zh: 練習只為了公開演出，不是為了學會困難的節拍。

scene.explanationZh: 最終流暢與初次自然上手是不同時間的資料；不能略過她明說的困難開始。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只從「She took to it like a duck to water」推論出來？

options.en: She seemed to adapt easily to the activity in that context.
options.zh: 她在那個情境中，顯得容易適應該活動。

options.en: She had already mastered every advanced task connected with the activity.
options.zh: 她已掌握與該活動相關的每項進階工作。

options.en: The context is needed to identify what it refers to.
options.zh: 需要情境，才知道 it 指甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 慣用語突出初步自然與容易；進階程度及活動範圍，需要另外交代。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「Jin 操作那麼自然，我就把取得公開許可的工作也交給他，不用再問了。」Jin 剛表示還不懂許可程序。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Jin took to it like a duck to water, but that was the recorder; let us explain the permission process before assigning that responsibility.
options.zh: Jin 很快便輕鬆上手，但那是錄音機操作；我們先解釋許可程序，再分配那項責任吧。

options.en: I would assign the permission task now because confidence with the controls should be enough preparation.
options.zh: 我會現在分配許可工作，因為有信心操作控制，應該就是足夠準備。

options.en: I would make Jin repeat the basic controls lesson rather than explain the separate permission process.
options.zh: 我會讓 Jin 重上基本控制課，而不解釋另一項許可程序。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可以肯定操作容易，也針對尚未學會的責任補充指導；不把一方面的順利當成另一任務已準備好，也不因另一項不熟悉，就只重教已會的操作。

speaking.en: I took to it like a duck to water when I first tried the simple controls, but I still asked for help with the unfamiliar settings.
speaking.zh: 我初次試用簡單控制便輕鬆上手，但仍就不熟悉的設定尋求協助。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清初次上手與仍待學習的部分。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在麵包工作坊很快學會摺麵團，身旁的初學者卻跟不上。你想承認自己上手容易，並請導師慢慢示範一次、讓對方重試，而不是替對方完成麵包。用一至兩句英文提出實際請求。

examples.en: I took to it like a duck to water, but the others may need a slower demonstration of the fold. Could we show it once more and let them try again rather than finish their loaves for them?
examples.zh: 我很快便輕鬆上手，但其他人可能需要較慢的摺麵團示範。我們可否再示範一次，讓他們重試，而不是替他們完成麵包？

examples.en: I seem to have taken to it like a duck to water, but I do not want my pace to set the pace for everyone. Could we pause for one slow fold and give the other beginners another attempt?
examples.zh: 我似乎很快便輕鬆上手，但不想用我的步伐決定所有人的節奏。我們可否停下來慢慢摺一次，讓其他初學者再試一次？

writing.selfCheckZh: 請求要有較慢示範及自己重試的機會；肯定自己的容易，不把它當作所有人都應同樣快，也不以代做取代對方的學習。

takeaways.en: She took to it like a duck to water when trying the weaving frame, then asked to learn how to repair a broken thread.
takeaways.zh: 她初次試用織架便輕鬆上手，之後再請人教她怎樣修補斷線。

takeaways.en: He had taken to it like a duck to water at the first rehearsal, though the later performance still required preparation.
takeaways.zh: 第一次排練時，他已輕鬆上手，但之後的演出仍需準備。

lessons.titleZh: 存在卻未受到注意的背景訊息

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: For her, the app was only background noise.

brief.meaningEn: Something present in a person’s surroundings or attention field but treated as unimportant and largely ignored.
brief.meaningZh: 存在於一個人周遭或可接觸範圍，卻被視為不重要而大致忽略的事物。
brief.grammar: become/be only background noise to/for someone. In this figurative use, specify what is ignored and by whom. The term also has a literal sound meaning, which context must distinguish.
brief.register: An ordinary sound noun extended to peripheral attention in the source app example. This lesson teaches that contextual image, not a claim that the words are a clinical or technical diagnosis.
brief.boundaryZh: 背景位置關乎注意力，不只關乎音量，也不能單憑被忽略便判定內容錯誤或不重要。
brief.misconceptionZh: 同一則訊息對某人是背景，對另一人可能很重要；需按人物、目的及當時注意的內容說明。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述有東西存在卻未受注意，並按溝通目的提出讓必要資訊清楚可見的方法。

listening.promptZh: 這裏的背景訊息，描述了怎樣的注意力安排？

options.en: The updates were present, but Lina’s attention was on her friend rather than their content.
options.zh: 更新存在，但 Lina 的注意力在朋友身上，不在更新內容。

options.en: Lina studied each new post and used it to question her friend’s account.
options.zh: Lina 仔細看了每則新帖文，並用它們追問朋友的敘述。

options.en: The feed had been closed before the circle, so no updates were present.
options.zh: 小組開始前動態已關閉，所以沒有更新出現。

options.en: The account establishes that the app’s announcements were factually incorrect.
options.zh: 敘述確立了，應用程式公布的內容事實上錯誤。

listening.explanationZh: 背景比喻指存在卻不在注意中心；敘述沒有證明帖文錯誤，也沒有說動態關閉。
listening.en: During the story circle, the app updates became background noise to Lina: the feed stayed open, but she followed her friend’s account and later could not say what the new posts had announced.
listening.zh: 說故事小組進行時，應用程式更新對 Lina 變成了未受注意的背景訊息：動態仍開著，但她專注朋友的敘述，之後說不出新帖文公布了甚麼。

reply.promptEn: Why could Lina not describe the new announcements afterwards?
reply.promptZh: Lina 之後為甚麼說不出新公布的內容？

options.en: The updates had become background noise while she concentrated on her friend’s story.
options.zh: 她專注朋友故事時，更新已變成未受注意的背景訊息。

options.en: She was following the spoken account rather than reading the feed.
options.zh: 她當時在聽敘述，沒有閱讀動態。

options.en: An open feed did not mean its contents held her attention.
options.zh: 動態開著，不表示內容吸引了她的注意。

options.en: The posts were present, but she had not been attending to what they said.
options.zh: 帖文存在，但她沒有留意上面說甚麼。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都用注意力去向解釋；不是單憑設備開著，就假定人已讀懂，也不是判斷公布內容的對錯。

scene.promptZh: 主持人輕聲說出新截止日期，大家都停下記錄，再確認所需步驟。旁人只因聲音小，就稱日期是沒人注意的背景訊息。哪句最好？

options.en: The date was spoken softly but actively noted, so low volume alone does not make it background noise in this figurative sense.
options.zh: 日期雖輕聲說出，卻受到主動注意，所以音量小本身，不會令它成為這個比喻中的背景訊息。

options.en: Speaking softly establishes that the listeners ignored the date.
options.zh: 輕聲說話確立了，聽眾忽略了日期。

options.en: The listeners treated the date as a familiar detail they did not need to record.
options.zh: 聽眾把日期當成不需記錄的熟悉資料。

scene.explanationZh: 敘述明說大家記錄並確認步驟；比喻中的忽略不能只按音量推斷。

contrast.promptZh: 在這個注意力比喻中，哪項最不能只從「The updates were background noise to her」得出？

options.en: She treated the updates as peripheral rather than her focus.
options.zh: 她把更新放在注意邊緣，而不是焦點。

options.en: The updates had been checked and found unreliable.
options.zh: 更新已核對，並被判定不可靠。

options.en: Another person might attend to the same updates differently.
options.zh: 另一人可能以不同方式注意相同更新。

contrast.explanationZh: 沒有注意與已核實不可靠不同；同一內容也可因人物及目的不同，而獲得不同注意。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「Lina 沒記住帖文，就表示公布是假的吧？」你只知道她在聽故事。哪個回應最好？

options.en: They were background noise to her at that moment; that tells us where her attention was, not whether the announcements were true.
options.zh: 當時那些更新對她只是背景訊息；這告訴我們她注意甚麼，不是公布是否真實。

options.en: I would use her inability to recall the posts as the reason to reject the announcements.
options.zh: 我會用她記不起帖文，作為否定公布的理由。

options.en: I would assume that leaving the feed open meant she had read the updates before listening to the story.
options.zh: 我會假定，動態開著就表示，她在聽故事前已讀過更新。

dialogue.explanationZh: 要把注意與真實性分開，也不能從畫面開著，補成已完成閱讀。

speaking.en: The repeated notices had become background noise to me, so I stopped and checked which date I actually needed to remember.
speaking.zh: 那些重複通知已變成我沒有注意的背景訊息，所以我停下來，核對究竟需要記住哪個日期。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清訊息存在與有沒有受到注意。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學生說，佈告板塞滿重複及已過期海報，重要活動截止日期常被忽略。你要請負責人整理資訊，不只是再貼更大的海報。用一至兩句英文寫實際請求，提出清走過期內容並保留一張有清楚日期的現行通知。

examples.en: The crowded board has become background noise, and students say they miss the deadline among the repeated posters. Could we remove the expired notices and keep one current notice with a clear due date?
examples.zh: 擁擠的佈告板已變成未受注意的背景訊息，學生說在重複海報之間，會漏看截止日期。我們可否清走過期通知，保留一張有清楚截止日期的現行通知？

examples.en: Adding another large poster may leave the board as background noise rather than help students find the date. Please clear the old notices and give the current deadline its own uncluttered space.
examples.zh: 再加一張大海報，可能仍令佈告板成為沒人注意的背景訊息，而沒有幫學生找到日期。請清走舊通知，給現行截止日期一處不擁擠的空間。

glossary.zh: 一處專屬而不擁擠的空間

writing.selfCheckZh: 請求要依學生回報說明被忽略的情況，再提出整理及清楚日期；不把問題只當成海報不夠大，也不假定訊息受忽略就不真實。

takeaways.en: The familiar slogan became background noise to him until a visitor asked what it meant in that particular exhibition.
takeaways.zh: 那句熟悉標語原本是他沒有注意的背景訊息，直到訪客問它在那個展覽裏有甚麼意思。

takeaways.en: She realised that the announcements had become background noise and asked the group which channel they would actually check for an urgent change.
takeaways.zh: 她發現公布已變成大家沒有注意的背景訊息，便問小組，遇到緊急改動時，實際會查看哪個途徑。

lessons.titleZh: 工作中按固定步驟處理的部分

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Software can handle the mechanical side of work.

brief.meaningEn: The routine part of work that follows established steps rather than requiring a fresh interpretation at each step.
brief.meaningZh: 工作中依循既定步驟、每一步不需重新作出詮釋的例行部分。
brief.grammar: the mechanical side of work/our work; mechanical contrasts with the particular judgement tasks described in context. A person can do routine work by hand, and using a computer does not make every task mechanical.
brief.register: The adjective has an established automatic or routine action sense; the whole noun phrase productively identifies a component of work, not a fixed occupational category. Mechanical can be dismissive in other contexts, so acknowledge the effort and importance of routine tasks.
brief.boundaryZh: 例行部分仍可能需要仔細、時間與核對；這裏的機械式不等於沒有價值，也不等於整份工作都不需判斷。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能把工具處理格式，說成已核實主張；也不能因某人做的是例行部分，就抹去其貢獻。
brief.outcomeZh: 能清楚劃分例行步驟與仍需判斷的部分，也準確肯定執行者的貢獻。

listening.promptZh: 程式處理了甚麼？哪項工作仍由人判斷？

options.en: It applied fixed naming and formatting rules, while people evaluated the conflicting accounts.
options.zh: 它套用固定命名及格式規則，而人則評估矛盾敘述。

options.en: It resolved the conflicting accounts before any person compared them.
options.zh: 任何人比較之前，它已解決了矛盾敘述。

options.en: The people checked only file names, while the script chose the report’s interpretation.
options.zh: 人只核對檔案名稱，程式則選擇報告的詮釋。

options.en: The list contained the final factual conclusion rather than naming and formatting rules.
options.zh: 清單包含最終事實結論，而不是命名及格式規則。

listening.explanationZh: 例行部分是按清單執行命名與格式；對矛盾資料的比較，仍另由人處理，不是格式完成便等於結論已核實。
listening.en: The script handled the mechanical side of our work by applying file names and caption formats from a fixed list; we still compared the conflicting accounts ourselves before deciding what the report could claim.
listening.zh: 程式按固定清單套用檔案名稱及圖說格式，處理我們工作中的例行部分；決定報告可以作甚麼主張之前，我們仍親自比較互相矛盾的敘述。

reply.promptEn: Why did you say the script handled only a routine part of the report work?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼說程式只處理報告工作的例行部分？

options.en: It handled the mechanical side of our work, following fixed names and formats rather than weighing the accounts.
options.zh: 它處理我們工作的例行部分，依循固定名稱及格式，而不是衡量敘述。

options.en: The naming list told it what to apply, while we still had to compare the evidence.
options.zh: 命名清單告訴它要套用甚麼，我們仍須比較證據。

options.en: Formatting completion did not decide which interpretation the report could support.
options.zh: 格式完成，沒有決定報告能支持哪種詮釋。

options.en: The task it performed was applying established rules, not resolving the conflicting statements.
options.zh: 它執行的是套用既定規則，不是解決互相矛盾的陳述。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以實際分工解釋例行範圍；不把完成固定步驟與作出資料判斷混在一起。

scene.promptZh: 作者在電腦上逐一比較兩份互相矛盾的訪問，考慮證據後決定應保留哪項未確定說法。旁人只因她用電腦，就稱這全是不用重新判斷的例行步驟。哪句最好？

options.en: Using a computer does not make this the mechanical side of work; she is weighing evidence rather than merely applying a fixed format.
options.zh: 使用電腦，不會令這變成工作中的例行部分；她在衡量證據，不只是套用固定格式。

options.en: The device establishes that she is following a predetermined interpretation without comparing accounts.
options.zh: 所用設備確立了，她在依循預定詮釋，沒有比較敘述。

options.en: The description says she has left the evidence review to a script and is checking only file names.
options.zh: 描述說，她把證據審閱交給程式，自己只核對檔案名稱。

scene.explanationZh: 分類應按實際認知工作，不只按使用的設備；比較矛盾資料與套用固定格式不同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 the mechanical side of work 在這裏的範圍？

options.en: Describe the repeatable steps that a fixed instruction list can specify.
options.zh: 描述可由固定指令清單列明的重複步驟。

options.en: Treat every task performed on a computer as requiring no interpretation.
options.zh: 把電腦上執行的每項工作，都視為不需詮釋。

options.en: Recognise that routine execution can still require care and deserve credit.
options.zh: 承認例行執行仍可能需要細心，也值得肯定。

contrast.explanationZh: 工作內容與設備不同；用電腦也可作詮釋，而按固定步驟做事仍有實際貢獻。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「格式都統一了，就把報告標成資料已核實吧？」你們尚未比較矛盾敘述。哪個回應最好？

options.en: The mechanical side of our work is done, but we still need to compare those accounts before marking the claims as checked.
options.zh: 我們工作的例行部分已完成，但把主張標成已核實之前，仍需比較那些敘述。

options.en: I would use consistent formatting as sufficient evidence that the different accounts agree.
options.zh: 我會把一致格式，當作不同敘述相符的充分證據。

options.en: I would finish the conclusion first and return to the contradictory details only if a reader challenges it.
options.zh: 我會先完成結論，等讀者提出質疑才回頭看矛盾細節。

dialogue.explanationZh: 格式完成只交代格式；結論需要按矛盾資料另作判斷，不能由外觀一致或等人質疑代替。

speaking.en: The mechanical side of our work involved copying agreed codes carefully, while the decision about which account to trust still needed discussion.
speaking.zh: 我們工作的例行部分，是仔細抄寫議定代碼；至於應信哪份敘述，仍需討論。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再按具體步驟區分例行處理與詮釋判斷。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：年刊完成後，你要在致謝中肯定 Mei 按既定編號逐份整理提交記錄的工作。這很例行，卻讓大家找得到檔案；她沒有負責審閱文章事實。用一至兩句英文寫實際致謝，具體肯定她，不把整理記錄說成已完成事實核對。

examples.en: Mei took care of the mechanical side of our work, carefully applying the agreed numbers to each submission record. Her patient work made the files easy to find, while the editors remained responsible for checking the articles.
examples.zh: Mei 照料我們工作的例行部分，仔細把議定編號套用到每份提交記錄。她耐心的工作讓檔案容易找到，文章核對則仍由編輯負責。

examples.en: We thank Mei for the mechanical side of the work: numbering the submission records consistently so that we could locate each file. This careful contribution supported the yearbook without taking over the editors’ factual review.
examples.zh: 我們感謝 Mei 處理工作的例行部分：為提交記錄一致編號，讓我們找得到每份檔案。這項細心貢獻支援年刊，但沒有接替編輯的事實審閱。

writing.selfCheckZh: 致謝要有可辨識的工作及實際幫助，也保留核對責任的分工；不貶低例行貢獻，也不給予沒有執行的事實審閱功勞。

takeaways.en: The mechanical side of the work took patience, so she thanked the person who had carefully transferred every agreed label.
takeaways.zh: 工作的例行部分需要耐心，所以她感謝仔細轉錄每個議定標籤的人。

takeaways.en: He separated the mechanical side of work from the choice of questions, then asked who would check each part before publication.
takeaways.zh: 他把工作的例行部分與問題選擇分開，再問公開發表前，由誰核對各部分。

lessons.titleZh: 協助掌舵的工作伙伴

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: AI may act as a co-pilot for the analyst.

brief.meaningEn: A supportive working partner, using an aviation role as an image for helping someone carry out a task.
brief.meaningZh: 以航空職位作意象，形容協助別人完成任務的工作伙伴。
brief.grammar: act as a co-pilot for someone; be my/our co-pilot. In the source work metaphor, describe the actual division of tasks. The metaphor alone does not specify every permission, skill or decision rule.
brief.register: Figurative extension of the aviation noun, not a claim that the task involves an aircraft or that a named product has particular capabilities. Literal co-pilots can have substantial duties; the agreed supporting role here is established by context.
brief.boundaryZh: 協助角色仍可有重要貢獻；誰作甚麼決定，需要按實際約定，不是單靠稱呼便確定所有責任。
brief.misconceptionZh: 有協助不表示可放棄核對；也不應把所有幫忙一概當成奪權，應說清需要甚麼支援。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用這個意象提出具體協助角色，並保留約定的發言、核對或決定責任。

listening.promptZh: 這個項目的協助與決定責任怎樣分配？

options.en: The tool suggested groupings, while Noor checked quotations and decided what to claim.
options.zh: 工具建議分組，Noor 則核對引文，並決定作甚麼主張。

options.en: The tool’s proposed grouping was automatically the report’s final conclusion.
options.zh: 工具提出的分組，自動就是報告的最終結論。

options.en: Noor’s only agreed job was to format a conclusion the tool had already approved.
options.zh: Noor 唯一議定工作，是為工具已批准的結論編排格式。

options.en: The project assigned quotation checking to the tool and grouping suggestions to Noor.
options.zh: 項目把引文核對分給工具，把分組建議分給 Noor。

listening.explanationZh: 角色由敘述中的分工確定：工具提出建議，Noor 核對並決定；不能倒轉工作，也不能把建議直接當成結論。
listening.en: In the fictional project, the tool was a co-pilot for Noor: it proposed groups for interview comments, while she checked the quotations and chose the report’s claims; a suggested grouping was not her final judgement.
listening.zh: 在這個虛構項目中，工具是 Noor 的協作助手：它提出訪問意見的分組，她則核對引文，並選擇報告的主張；建議分組不是她的最終判斷。

reply.promptEn: Why did Noor still check the quotations herself?
reply.promptZh: Noor 為甚麼仍親自核對引文？

options.en: The tool was a co-pilot, and their arrangement left her responsible for checking the material behind the claims.
options.zh: 工具是協作助手，而安排仍由她負責核對主張背後的資料。

options.en: A proposed grouping did not establish that each quotation had been represented accurately.
options.zh: 建議分組，沒有確立每段引文都已準確呈現。

options.en: She was the person assigned to choose what the report could claim.
options.zh: 她是被分配決定報告可作甚麼主張的人。

options.en: The agreed support did not replace her review of the underlying words.
options.zh: 議定的支援，沒有取代她審閱原來字句的工作。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都按已說明的核對及決定責任回答；不是聲稱所有叫作 co-pilot 的角色，在所有情境都只有相同權限。

scene.promptZh: 朋友把工具稱為「協作助手」，但實際安排是工具選所有結論，他不看引文，只按確認。你要指出這與他先前說好「由自己核對並決定」不一致，而非否認工具可有任何幫助。哪句最好？

options.en: Calling it a co-pilot does not establish the review he described; his actual process leaves the claims unchecked by him.
options.zh: 稱它為協作助手，不能確立他所說的審閱已有進行；實際流程中，他沒有核對主張。

options.en: The supporting label establishes that he has already compared the quotations himself.
options.zh: 協助的稱呼確立了，他已親自比較引文。

options.en: Any tool suggestion would prevent him from making a considered judgement of his own.
options.zh: 工具的任何建議，都會阻止他作出自己深思後的判斷。

scene.explanationZh: 要比較稱呼與實際分工；沒有自行核對與無法接受任何幫助，是不同事情。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只從「She asked me to be a co-pilot for the presentation」確定？

options.en: She is using a partnership image to ask for support.
options.zh: 她正以伙伴意象請求支援。

options.en: The exact speaking, checking and decision duties have already been specified by the label alone.
options.zh: 單憑稱呼，已列明準確的發言、核對及決定職責。

options.en: A discussion can clarify what support would actually help.
options.zh: 可以透過討論，釐清甚麼支援實際有幫助。

contrast.explanationZh: 意象可提出協助，但具體責任仍需交代；不能用稱呼代替分工。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「既然工具是助手，它整理完，我就不用看引文了吧？」你們已約定由人核對。哪個回應最好？

options.en: It can be a co-pilot, but our agreement still puts quotation checks with us; let us review the passages before accepting the groupings.
options.zh: 它可以是協作助手，但約定仍由我們核對引文；接受分組之前，我們先審閱段落吧。

options.en: I would accept the groups first and check the quotations only if the final headings look confusing.
options.zh: 我會先接受分組，只在最終標題看起來混亂時，才核對引文。

options.en: I would reject the suggestions before reading them because accepting help would mean giving up our own judgement.
options.zh: 我會未看便拒絕建議，因為接受幫助就等於放棄自己的判斷。

dialogue.explanationZh: 按約定使用支援並完成核對，才能保持清楚責任；外觀順暢不能代替證據，也不用把接受建議當成放棄判斷。

speaking.en: Could you be my co-pilot for the rehearsal, keeping the question list while I speak and telling me afterwards where the explanation was unclear?
speaking.zh: 你可否做我的排練協作伙伴，在我說話時保管問題清單，之後告訴我哪裏解釋不清楚？
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再用具體動作說清想要的支援。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你答應在朋友外出時幫展覽核對作品編號與圖說，稱自己是他的協作伙伴。主辦者現在請你代選哪些作品撤下，但你未獲這項藝術決定權。你想向朋友釐清原約定，並請他指定無法即時聯絡時由誰決定。用一至兩句英文寫實際訊息，不假裝協作稱呼已授予所有權限。

examples.en: I agreed to be a co-pilot for checking the labels, not for removing any pieces from the exhibition. Could you confirm who should make that decision if the organiser asks while I cannot reach you?
examples.zh: 我答應做協作伙伴，核對標示，不是決定從展覽撤下作品。如果主辦者詢問時，我無法聯絡你，你可否確認應由誰作那項決定？

examples.en: I am happy to remain your co-pilot on the numbers and captions, but choosing which work stays goes beyond our original agreement. Please name someone who can make that decision during your absence, or tell the organiser which requests should wait for you.
examples.zh: 我願意繼續當你的協作伙伴，核對編號及圖說，但選哪些作品留下，超出原本約定。請指定你不在時可作決定的人，或告訴主辦者哪些要求應等你回來。

writing.selfCheckZh: 訊息要準確保留原有核對支援，說清新增決定超出約定，再要求可執行的替代決策安排；不把協作稱呼當成全面授權，也不一概拒絕原先答應的幫忙。

takeaways.en: The volunteer became a co-pilot for the workshop, tracking the materials while the tutor led the demonstrations under their agreed plan.
takeaways.zh: 義工成為工作坊的協作伙伴，按議定計劃記錄材料，導師則帶領示範。

takeaways.en: She asked her co-pilot to note the unanswered questions so they could decide together which point needed another explanation.
takeaways.zh: 她請協作伙伴記下未回答的問題，讓兩人一起決定哪點需要再解釋。
